The perfection of the adamantine body of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, and the manifestation of the diverse bodies of the world—including gods and asuras—having entered the vast wilderness of wandering saṃsāra, all this is born of karma; it is bound by what is auspicious and inauspicious.

In this regard, no agent, doer, Lord (Īśvara), primordial matter (Pradhāna), or the Puruṣa projected by the Sāṅkhyas operates therein. With the sole exception of that which is born of karma, everything produced by the conditions of karma depends upon a cause, and that cause in turn depends upon conditions.

In this way, the condition of dependent origination connects with another, and through the accumulation of phlegm, it generates the great elements that bring about the formation of the primary elements; and those great elements proceed toward another aggregate from a beginningless course of existence, and having entered, they are reborn in various other destinations according to their detailed classification.
The fire of the knowledge of the obstruction and reversal of other times completely incinerates the latent predispositions (*vāsanā*) constructed by karma.
The equality of the three vehicles brings about the transcendence of the non-proliferated state (*niṣprapañcatā*).

The self-arisen knowledge of the Pratyekabuddhas of the Middle Period, who possess the rhinoceros-like [solitary] vehicle, proceeds from their own karma accumulated over the long duration of the Mahāyāna.

For those Śrāvakas who follow the sound of another's voice, their sovereignty over the realm is brief and of short duration; therefore, for the ignorant and deluded, their intellect functions only toward other dharmas that do not proceed beyond that. Furthermore, this arrangement of the world, produced by various karmas and characterized by its specific regions and dress, looks toward the auspicious, ageless perfection—the accomplishment of a world of karma that is sorrowless and stainless.
It performs only karma—pure, free from the [wrong] path, endowed with the eight limbs, and most cooling—and it does not depend on any other karma.
Freed from both action and non-action, he remains beyond conceptual proliferation;
yet, as long as one proceeds by means of the three vehicles, no other peace arises.
Mantra is indeed threefold, and action is proclaimed to be threefold;
the accomplishment of the fruit is threefold, and the investigation is likewise threefold.
The opposite action is likewise seen to be threefold;
that is declared to be the threefold wholesome, as it is further observed in the Tantra.
Furthermore, such a lineage is the peaceful locus of mantras;
indeed, the lineage of the Buddhas is the peaceful, pure-minded lineage of nirvāṇa.
That very same action is proclaimed as the portion belonging to the mantra-limb;
likewise, the jyotiṣa-limb is established in the world for the sake of accomplishment. Indeed, that very portion of action proceeds within the portion of conviction.
Just as rice grains are identified by their sprout,
so too are perfected substances identified by their characteristic mark.
Just as the color white is conceptually constructed through conventional usage,
so too are the methods of astrology conceptualized for the sake of conventional usage;
thus, among all methods, action alone is praised in every respect.
That karma does not exist anywhere without signs; nor does the body persist without signs, nor without conduct, nor without birth-accounts based on one's lineage.
That action is constantly perceived through various signs;
nowhere is action observed as a distinct entity, for it remains hidden within.
Just as a living being afflicted with fever is perceived by its various symptoms,
so too is the karma of embodied beings seen as it has fully entered their bodies.
The Jātaka treatises, which indicate the signs of auspicious and inauspicious fruits, have been proclaimed;
likewise, there are various birds and beings that arise from various types of karma.
Likewise, the time of birth, journeys, and the various cries of living beings always yield auspicious or inauspicious results.
One observes the signs of success and failure for the sake of conviction;
a sign is defined as conduct or a mark that serves as a basis for conviction.
Therefore, with every effort,
one who recites the mantra should depend upon the conditions for the sake of attaining success in the mantra.
One should observe these various personal karmas for their integrity;
indeed, that which is not observed will surely be beset by most terrible obstructive actions.
"Therefore, all these are limbs"—this was the word of the Sage;
thus the omniscient Sālendrarāja entered the seat of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa).
He uttered a mantra that destroys all obstacles and annihilates bad dreams, ill omens, and what is difficult to endure.
When the mind of that great-souled one, who was intent on awakening, was directed toward omniscience, Māra, with a wicked heart, created a most terrifying obstacle.
By him, indeed, was seen at the foot of the tree that great terror which is signless;
from that signlessness there arose for him many forms of dread.
Through the empowerment of his merit, which had been long desired by him,
that power of the mantra then shattered Namuci’s hopes.
Possessing supernatural powers and great heroism, he is self-restrained and of great splendor;
through the power of his mantra, I seek supreme enlightenment.
That very mantra will be taught for the destruction of ill omens,
as well as for [overcoming] unbearable bad dreams and the warding off of malevolent beings.
Let the hosts of gods indeed listen to this king of mantras, which was formerly spoken by the Jina Śālendra, the lord of the luminaries of the planets and constellations.
And for the purpose of subduing the wicked, she is the one who governs the planets, lunar mansions, and stars;
she is the manifestation of all elemental beings, possessing a gentle mind and awakening others.

Let all the hosts of spirits hear, whoever they may be that roam the earth— whether footless, many-footed, two-footed, or four-footed; let all beings in brief, whatever they may be, including those that are stationary in the three realms, listen.
Homage to all Buddhas, whose teachings are unimpeded.
Oṃ kha kha khāhi khāhi / hūṃ hūṃ / jvala jvala /
Blaze, blaze!
Stand firm, stand firm!
Ṣṇīḥ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā!
This mantra, empowered by the Buddha, is proclaimed as the Jvāloṣṇīṣa.
He who is honored as the embodiment of all auspiciousness performs eighty-five thousand various rites;
by a single recitation, he destroys evil dreams and ill omens.
He performs other rites as the master of all mantras;
he has mastery over all sentient beings, for this Buddha is the source and the teacher.
By the recollection of this mantra, all obstacles are destroyed;
having thus spoken, "O Buddha, the God of Gods," the best of sages [concluded].
They stood silent for a moment, awaiting the proper time;
and then the hosts of gods remained stationed above the Śuddhāvāsa realm.
Terrified, they all went to the assembly of the chief gods, the lunar mansions, the planets, and the stars; the Uṣṇīṣas were addressed with mantras.
Equal in power, of great heroism, known as the Uṣṇīṣa, and possessing great radiance;
[the mantras consist of] five hundred, four hundred, seven, eight, or ninety syllables.
Sixty-two and another seventy-five are proclaimed as the Uṣṇīṣendras;
this number is incalculable, for these auspicious kings are born from the hair of the head.
This mantra is equal to them, for it is born from the hair of the Victor’s head.

Thus concludes the fifteenth chapter, the detailed section on the conditions of one’s own karma, from the *Āryamañjuśrīmūlakalpa*, an extensive Mahāyāna sūtra that is an ornament of the Bodhisattva-piṭaka.
Now begins the eighteenth detailed section.
Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, having again gazed upon the abode of the Pure Abodes (*śuddhāvāsabhavana*) and that circle of the assembly, addressed Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta:

"Mañjuśrī, there exists for a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is devoted to your mantra practice and intends to fulfill the conduct of a bodhisattva, a detailed exposition of chapters on the methods suitable for the sequence of ritual actions, the sequence of yoga, and the practice of yoga in accordance with the movement of the constellations, which serve as the means for accomplishing the purpose of all mantra practices. I shall speak it; listen to it, and attend to it well and thoroughly."
When the Blessed One had spoken thus, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta said this to the Blessed One:

"It is wonderful, Blessed One, how the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas have been favored with the supreme favor by what has been spoken! [Speak] for the sake of compassion toward us, concerning those beings who follow all the practices of a Bodhisattva and who fulfill the purpose of all mantra-practices."
Thus addressed, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, with palms joined in reverence, gazed at the Blessed One and remained there in silence.
Then indeed, the Blessed One Śākyamuni, desiring to benefit the world,
spoke these supreme words of Vajrendra for the welfare of all embodied beings.
O noble friends, this is the most excellent constellation, beneficial or harmful, for all the practice of the purpose of mantras; it is appropriate or inappropriate for those who are composed.
One should describe the goal as accomplished, likewise fulfilled, and favorable;
for the sake of attaining success, the practitioner of mantra should thus characterize the mantra according to the tantra.
On a pure day, in a pure place, always delighting in pure conduct,
on an auspicious lunar day and asterism, he should always remain pure during the bright fortnight.

Having bathed, being meditative, observant of vows, and proficient in mantras, one who is skilled in the meaning of the mantra-tantras should perform the fire sacrifice (homa), recitation (japa), and likewise the accomplishment of the ritual in full detail.
Revatī, Phalgunī, Citrā, Maghā, and Puṣya are conducive to the accomplishment of one's aims;
likewise, Anurādhā, Jyeṣṭhā, and Mūlā are also described as such.
Both Āṣāḍhas and both Bhādrapadas are always for the sake of accomplishment; Śravaṇā is for the sake of accomplishment, and Dhaniṣṭhā is also described as excellent for the sake of accomplishment.
Likewise, for the sake of accomplishment, [one should act] with mantras under the constellations Rohiṇī, Mṛgaśiras, Aśvinī,
Punarvasu, Svāti, and Revatī.
For these are praised and reckoned as being intent upon the practice of the sciences;
for them, Monday is declared to be the prescribed day.

During the cool season, one should perform rites for pacification; thereafter, during the remaining times, one should perform those for the sake of knowledge and nourishment. At midday, when the sun is present, the rite is performed; it is also forbidden when the moon is present.
When the moon stands at midnight, one should perform rites of sorcery;
when the third watch has arrived, one should commence [rites] for the sake of prosperity.
One should accomplish the mantra for the sake of nourishment or for the purpose of enjoyment among men;
one should know the rising sun through proper application in all ritual actions.
Likewise, in the absence of red [substances], one should perform the rite of malevolent magic (abhicāruka) during the time of the sun;
one should know that this occurs at the remaining time, specifically in the forenoon within the solar disc.
Likewise, for the rite of pacification (śāntika), one should always perform it when [the shadow] has risen to the measure of a yoke;
thereafter, the measurement for Gabhastin should be known as two cubits.
One should perform pacifying rites when engaged in pacifying activities,
using the most excellent mantras and mudrās originating from the foremost family of the Victors.
When the sun has reached midday, one should perform rites of sorcery (ābhicāruka);
thereafter, for the purpose of subjugation (vaśya), one should employ [the rite] for attraction (ākṛṣya).
When the sun has reached the afternoon and is lowered by the distance of a yoke,
one should perform all rites, as well as those joined for minor purposes.
Thereafter, at a later time, those wise ones then performed all the rites of subjugation and attraction directed toward the Sun.
When the sun has set, possessing a radiance equal to the color of blood,
one should perform those rites that arise with a similar reddish luster.
Those who desire a lover should always perform actions with passion; however, it is taught that an action resulting in the destruction of even the three lineages is censurable.
One who desires a maiden should quickly perform the rite as prescribed for the appropriate time;
then, during the first watch of the night, one should accomplish the ritual while joined with the spirit of a sentient being.
From this point onward, one should cause all rites to be performed everywhere.
Then, at midnight, the Moon-graha shall behold the earth.
At that time, when it has risen together with him, one should enter the western regions;
thereafter, the planet shall behold the sun along with the lord of men.
One who seeks success, having applied the mantra at the time of childbirth,
shall swiftly obtain abundant accomplishment of their purpose even in the mortal world.
Both the non-reciter and the reciter obtain their fruit;
the wise reciter likewise accomplishes whatever siddhi he desires.
In the third watch, one should always proceed with diligence toward the southern-western direction; one should go there, for it is the source of the fruit.
Likewise, when the sun rises toward the northern direction,
and thereafter, at the end of time, when the sun has risen for the duration of a yuga;
The knower of the tantras should go to the intermediate direction that arises from the fruit of the desired accomplishments; that region is proclaimed to be between the west and the north.
The Tathāgatas have taught the method for both the non-reciter and the reciter;
it is prescribed for the accomplishment of the task when the mantra has been mastered.
At midday, one should go toward the east and in all directions;
thereafter, one should cause the ritual acts to be performed.
Then, at midnight, the planet Candra beheld the earth at the end of time and at the edge of the intermediate directions, O Sage, through awakening.
For those desiring accomplishment, [the site] between the east and the north is similar;
beyond that, the directions are said to be [situated] between the east and the south at all times.
The divisions of time and the directions, as well as the intermediate points, have been described; thus, in the afternoon, one should enter the abode of the Daityas when the sun is there.
And in all the subterranean tunnels, among the beings dwelling in wells, and in every way among those residing in the various regions of Pātāla that have glorious entrances; everywhere.
Then, at the end of the next watch, when the circle of planets has a reddish hue,
one should enter the abodes of the yakṣa species, which are indeed most terrifying.
One should quickly go to the dwelling place appointed for those times;
rising up, one should accomplish the mantra that arises from the foundation of grace.
Desiring to ascend to the very summit, whether for failure or indeed for success,
the daughter of Manu ascended to her own dwelling upon the roof of the palace.
For one who has reflected upon the Siddhānta and is well-engaged in it at the proper times,
the accomplishment of mantra will always be attained by those who are experts in the mantras and tantras.
By merely traveling in the [proper] direction, even a man who is not a practitioner of mantra quickly attains the full measure of accomplishment consisting of the arising of fruits.

One should accomplish desired objectives, both those pertaining to the villages and those concerning human beings; the times have been declared according to the sacred tradition, as well as the directions in every respect.
The mantra-practitioner may produce [results] everywhere, at these times and in these places:
namely, when Aśvinī is conjoined with Bharaṇī, as well as Kṛttikā and Mṛgaśiras.
Indeed, when applied to all these very lunar mansions,
the rite for pacification is prescribed as that which brings about the perfect arising of both cause and fruit.
One who desires prosperity should always accomplish his aims under Rohiṇī while engaged in recitation;
under Ārdrā, one should perform rites for the purpose of subjugation and attraction.
Likewise, under Punarvasu and Puṣya, one should accomplish the attainment of wealth,
as well as various ornaments, garments, collyrium, and realgar.

One should employ yellow pigment (rocanā), red ochre (gairika), and well-consecrated clarified butter (ājya) under the Puṣya asterism for the purposes of subjugation, attraction, and the enhancement of intelligence.
Likewise, under Āśleṣā, one should perform the act of drawing a weapon;
and under Maghā, one should perform the act that increases sovereignty and wealth.
Both Phalgunīs, the most excellent, mounted their own vehicle;
for it is by the hand alone that various deeds are performed.
One should perform activities involving wealth and ritual action under Svāti and Viśākhā;
likewise, both Anurādhā and Jyeṣṭhā are joined with these lunar mansions.
One desiring success should always perform it, as should one desiring sovereignty;
likewise, one desiring various earthly riches and the highest excellence born of one's lineage.
When applied to the lunar mansions (nakṣatras), they bring about the accomplishment of wealth;
for both Aṣāḍhās are likewise declared to be employed in rites concerning living beings,
and success is seen in all matters regarding metals as well.
One who is skilled in mantras and tantras should perform root-rites and various medicinal preparations at the root asterism, when the moon is conjoined with that asterism.
Everywhere during the month of Śrāvaṇa, one should perform the rites described for Śrāvaṇī;
furthermore, one should apply oneself to the Dharma that leads to Nirvāṇa and also to the life of renunciation.
One who knows the ritual procedures should always perform the accomplishment of incense, lotuses, trees, vehicles, and garments during the Dhaniṣṭhā asterism.
One may indeed perform cruel acts of violence against living beings during Śatabhiṣaj;
however, one should avoid that contemptible act when it involves the deprivation of life from sentient beings.
Both Bhadrapadas are excellent and ward off calamities on earth;
indeed, when employed in rites, they swiftly bring about prosperity.
In accomplishing the goals of generalship,
in the kingdom, in the production of wealth, and in ornaments such as jewelry and the like.
One who is knowledgeable in mantras and tantras should accomplish various groups of elements according to their desires, joined with both lunar mansions.
Under the asterism Revatī, one should accomplish the acquisition of wealth arising from various minerals;
one should accomplish mantra-rites arising from various jewels;
and the knower of mantras should always accomplish all kinds of waters.
Aśvinī, Bharaṇī, and a portion of Kṛttikā—
this is declared to be the domain of Aṅgāraka (Mars) in the firmament.
Then, one should accomplish her day, as well as her gentle fame and the earth;
one should know Kṛttikā to consist of three parts, while Rohiṇī and Mṛgaśiras are the subsequent two.
One should know this regarding Bhārgava;
likewise, in the vault of the sky, the portion of Mṛgaśiras and Ārdrā are well-conjoined in this manner.
Furthermore, one should know that Punarvasu is for the sake of peace; likewise, Kṣetrabhava, Puṣyāṅga, Āśleṣā, and Maghā are also understood [to serve that purpose].
This field of the Sun always brings about malevolent magic; both [the fields] under Phalgunī, marked by the signs of the planets, are likewise effective when accompanied by their respective limbs.
One should know Induvāra to be likewise; its field is in Niśākara.
One should perform the highly esteemed rite when Hasta and Citrā, along with their respective portions, are present.
He is declared to be situated in the station of Mercury, the accomplisher of all rites;
he is also proclaimed to be conjoined with Svāti and Viśākhā, or even with their degrees.
The second field is undoubtedly designated as belonging to the Sun;
Anurādhā and Jyeṣṭhā are those two portions designated for the Son of the Earth (Mars).
The second field of Mars arises from Scorpio;
endowed with all dharmas and purposes, it accomplishes the goals associated with one's actions.
The wise man should avoid violence and the desire to perform malevolent rites that harm living beings;
instead, he should accomplish various goals and abundant ritual actions.
Likewise, Mūla and Āṣāḍhā are both declared to arise from the three portions [of the asterisms];
this is the field of Bṛhaspati, which, though situated in the sky, is seen upon the earth.
With a disciplined mind, one should accomplish the ritual according to the injunctions, thereby attaining the removal of obstacles,
the attainment of great enjoyments and wealth, and the fruitful emergence of results.
One indicated by the asterism Dhanvin (Sarpa) shall bring about all prosperity;
those indicated by Śravaṇā and Dhaniṣṭhā are declared to be equal to Śatabhiṣā.
This second field of Śaniścara has been described in the past;
it is designated as the sign Capricorn and is the dispeller of all misfortunes.
If a wise knower of mantras, staying there, should undertake ritual actions, they will succeed without effort when performed at that time.
The asterisms designated as Kumbha were proclaimed by the sages of old;
both Bhadrapadas are renowned, as is the illustrious Revatī.
Likewise, the eastern quarter, even if deficient in limbs, is auspicious if marked by benefic and Jupiter planets; all such excellent [directions] should be given as a field to the preceptor.
Thus has been described in summary the Pisces sign, marked by worldly characteristics;
the planet is everywhere predominant, whether moving horizontally or ascending in all activities.
These seven have indeed been described as the foremost among the hosts of non-humans at the onset of planetary influence.
While the chief planets are infinite and the contemptible planets are likewise infinite,
these [seven] are declared to be neutral, bringing both benefit and harm to human beings.
Thus,
regarding those practitioners of mantra-recitation, the application of sentient beings has been explained;
likewise, the presence or absence of sentient beings, as well as the time and the specific rule, have been proclaimed.
There is no grasping associated with the Dharma, nor is there action marked by the planets;
the conjunction of the planets and constellations is declared to be the accomplishment of mantra.
Success is not to be known as time, nor is failure said to be time;
both of these, success and failure, arise sequentially from attachment and time.
Those who delight in the contrary are not practitioners of the Dharma; they are not followers of the Dharma.
One who is joined through the union of dharma and action will achieve success;
however, one who is devoid of action does not succeed by fate alone, for success does not arise from fate.
Both that action and its accomplishment depend solely upon destiny;
for there is no action apart from destiny, and destiny is nothing other than action.
But it is considered that the action is declared by the cause specified in the ritual rules;
for the planets are liberated from karma when the lunar mansions are well-worshipped.
Therefore, their action is equal; success is desired for the sake of action.
For these calculations have been taught, and action itself is always accompanied by the deities.
Neither the planets, nor the zodiac signs, nor the birth-constellations, even when well-honored, [determine one's fate];
one should always know that it is karma which is the cause, arising in accordance with the laws of destiny.
The arising of results is always dependent upon action; this is the principle taught regarding mantras.
Therefore, action arises from such principles, and not from planetary influences nor from the birth zodiac signs.
In brief, the course and origin of the constellations and lunar days,
as well as the regulation of the measure of time, are always dependent on the two types of karma and nothing else.
Therefore, one who knows the tantras should employ only that which is truly dharmic;
for in this world, there are various other multitudes of infinite malevolent spirits.
The lunar days have been calculated in battle by the commanders, as has the terrain;
therefore, I shall speak in brief—listen to what is being said.
Aries, Taurus, Gemini, and well-yoked Cancer;
and likewise Leo, Virgo, Libra, as well as Scorpio and Sagittarius.
The Makara and Kumbha are to be known [as such], while the Mīna and Vānara are the others;
the Mānuṣa and Devarāśi are another pair, as are the Garuḍa and Aparau.

The hosts of yakṣas and rākṣasas, as well as animals, pretas, and others who are auspicious, and the hells— these are designated as the infinite classes of rebirths born from the various modes of existence.
All the aggregates (rāśis) arising from various elements have been taught;
the sages have declared that these aggregates are innumerable and further categorized in many other ways.
I shall explain the signs of their courses and the basis for the birth-places of sentient beings; I shall speak of the infinite lunar mansions and planets,
and of the many fields described as being inhabited by various planets.

Thus ends the second chapter, the section on the knowledge of astrology regarding the characteristics of planets, lunar mansions, fields, and luminaries, from the *Āryamañjuśrīmūlakalpa*, a chapter-division from the sixteenth [chapter] of the *Mahāyāna-vaipulya-sūtra* which is an ornament of the *Bodhisattvapiṭaka*.
Now begins the nineteenth chapter-division.

Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, having again gazed upon the abode of the Pure Abodes (Śuddhāvāsabhavana), addressed Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta: "Mañjuśrī, there is a third chapter concerning the rules for the knowledge of astrology, which was spoken and approved by the previous Perfectly Awakened Ones, and which is fashioned according to the purpose of your mantra-tantras.
Listen well, pay close attention, and take it to heart."

When the Blessed One Śākyamuni had spoken thus, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta rose from his seat, draped his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee upon the ground, and with palms joined toward the Blessed One, addressed him as follows:
"It would be well, Blessed One, if you would explain the detailed exposition of the knowledge of astrology;
that will be for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of sentient beings."

For gods and humans, and for all beings who have entered into the practice of mantras, as well as those who have set out toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, they will easily accomplish the practice of mantras through skillful means.

This includes that which is favorable to all sentient beings, the performance of rites according to the rules of yoga, the ripening of karma resulting from the determination of time, and the convergence of constellations, days of the week, planets, birth-classes, fields, and zodiac signs.

That shall be a means for accomplishing happiness, a following of mantras with a happy maturation; that shall be the miraculous power and the sustaining grace of the playful transformations of those bodhisattvas.
When Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta had spoken thus, the Blessed One then said this to Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta:
"Excellent, excellent, Mañjuśrī! That you ask the Tathāgata about this matter—therefore, listen well and attend to it thoroughly."
"I shall speak for the benefit of all sentient beings.
When this had been said, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta prostrated at the feet of the Blessed One and sat down to listen to the Dharma.
Then the Blessed One, having pervaded the entire abode of the Śuddhāvāsa gods with his radiance, entered the samādhi called "The Illumination that Beholds All Buddhas.
Immediately upon the Blessed One’s entering this state, rays of light—blue, yellow, white, madder-red, crystal-colored, and so forth—issued forth from his body.

Having emerged and illuminated the buddha-fields of sentient beings, and having illuminated all the planets, constellations, birth-sources, lunar mansions, stars, and celestial abodes, as well as the dwellings of those in the realms of hell, animals, hungry ghosts, gods, and humans situated in the expanse of the sky, and having stilled all sufferings, it once again vanished into the work of the Blessed One Śākyamuni for the sake of all sentient beings.
Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, having arisen from that samādhi, addressed all those assemblies of deities of the lunar mansions, planets, and constellations:

"Listen, you assemblies of all the lunar mansion deities! Whoever has entered into the practice of mantras within this Dharma and Vinaya, and seeks to accomplish [the goal] here in this detailed ritual manual among all mantras, all substances, and the procedures for rites—you must not create obstacles therein. All of you, having assembled, must declare your presence and provide protection through the performance of guardian rites."

For whoever should transgress this pledge, Yamāntaka, the King of Wrath, would instantly summon all the lunar mansions and planets—those residing in infinite world-systems, along with their sons, kinsmen, and retinues. Standing upon the heads of them all and treading upon them with his foot, he would display various miraculous feats of fierce activity. By the empowerment of the Buddha, he would deprive them of life and establish them in the pledge. He would manifest himself in a transformed form, and at the end, all the hosts of spirits, yakṣas, rākṣasas, lunar mansions, planets, and constellations, as well as the groups of *nisattvas*, garuḍas, maruts, and mahoragas, being terrified and trembling, uttering great cries of distress and shaking, fell at the feet of the Blessed One and said: "Save us, Blessed One! Save us!"
“O Sugata, we are without a protector; we are without refuge. O Great King of Wrath, terrified with fear, may the Blessed One grant us our lives!
Having spoken thus, they became silent, their limbs trembling.
Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni addressed that assembly of constellations and planets, as well as the hosts of yakṣas, rākṣasas, pretas, piśācas, and mātṛs:
"Do not fear, sirs! Do not fear, sirs! For those who have approached the presence of the Tathāgatas, there is neither fear nor death."

For all sufferings can indeed be warded off, O friends: one should go for refuge to the Buddha; one should go for refuge to the Dharma, the foremost among all that protects from calamity; one should go for refuge to the Saṅgha, the foremost among those free from passion. For one who goes to the foremost of assemblies, there shall be no bristling of the hair [with fear]. One who truly desires the word of reality should be regarded as already liberated from the fear of death and from all fears and sufferings;
for him, no worldly fear ever exists.
May they attain that state which is the pacification of suffering, tranquility, freedom from fever, well-restrained, and directed toward enlightenment.

Then, at that very moment, by means of his supernatural power (*ṛddhi*), the Blessed One caused all their sufferings to be pacified; and Yamāntaka, the King of Wrath, prostrated at the feet of the Blessed One and sat down near Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta to listen to the Dharma.
And all those hosts of planets and constellations, as well as all their sufferings, were completely stilled.

And all the banners were stilled; they sat down to listen to the Dharma, composed, with one-pointed minds, gazing at the Blessed One, their eyes wide with wonder, and their hearts became filled with double joy.

Then the Blessed One, out of compassion for the world, gave a teaching of the Dharma in such a manner that it was associated with the Four Noble Truths, such that by those beings some perceived the Truths, some attained Arhatship, some realized Pratyekabuddhahood, and some generated the resolve for unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment; and all were rendered destined for unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. By all of them, the gates to rebirth among gods and humans were opened, while the doors to the lower realms, evil destinies, and perdition were closed, and the bolt of heaven was cast aside.
And all empower the pledge.

Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, having understood their underlying tendencies and knowing that the time for their conversion had arrived, immediately spoke the Dharma to those beings who were ready to be disciplined.
Overcome by the suffering of enemies, devoid of refuge, and born of faults— O hosts of gods, all such non-existence is honored here in this teaching.
Exert supreme vigor for the sake of the steps to enlightenment;
thus, O assemblies, you shall surely attain the abode that is peaceful and free from fever.
It is sorrowless, stainless, secure, and the ultimate nirvāṇa;
it is called the immaculate, equal to space, and the non-existence that is the true nature of reality.

"You shall attain the supreme, blameless, divine, well-frequented, and unobstructed state. By meditating throughout the day upon everything as impermanent, suffering, empty in meaning, and selfless— as it has been fully explained— they shall indeed attain the ultimate goal."
Through the designation of mantra and tantra, the practice that gives rise to bliss has been taught by the supreme Victors; it is declared to be the most excellent, the accomplishment of mantra.
The wise ones have taught the accomplishment of mantra as the foremost means for sentient beings, through their firm application, at the time of the fruit when there is a perfect convergence.
The variety of births is joined by the variety of actions;
from action comes varied accomplishment, for the manifold world is born from action as its source.
Variegated by means of these mantras in their variegated forms, the extensive ritual activities possess variegated purposes; thus, it is called "variegated action."
Karma is thus both conceivable and inconceivable; it is thought of as manifold and yet also as inconceivable.
Therefore, the practitioner of mantra should undertake abundant success within the various applications of mantra.
The zodiac signs have been described; men born under them are always [diverse], as are the various living beings and birds, including the foremost among gods and asuras.
And one should apply their respective signs to the attainments;
likewise, whether they be humans or celestial beings, those born under the sign of Aries [should be treated thus].
A man praised among women is born with many children, is eloquent, possesses a handsome form, is virtuous as a merchant, and is likewise brave.
A king who is crooked and of greedy mind, serving his household—Candramas is said to be situated there; one should employ him in all undertakings.
If the sun should be seen situated in the zodiac sign of Aries,
there, a rite joined with cruel actions will always achieve success.

One who knows the tantras and mantras should never resort to vehicles, walking, sitting, or lying down that are contrary to all yogis. A mortal born therein should always bestow the mantra for malevolent rites (*abhicāruka*).
A person born at that time in the zodiac sign of Taurus is always possessed of enjoyments;
he is ever beloved by women, yet greedy, and a judge of righteousness and unrighteousness.
The one who frequents the village, the ever-supervisor, let him understand the limbs of the god;
stationed there, he became the Moon, that righteous lord of the gods.
His mind should always be focused upon the kingdom;
to him, the mantras spoken by the Jina at the caityas should always be given.

By that [ascendant] conjoined with the Moon for the sake of the matter, the support of the person is understood from the matter; likewise, coming and going, as well as the act of shaving, are determined through logical reasoning.
One should perform the rites of the planets, but one should not engage in malevolent magic;
rather, one should apply oneself to all ritual activities that bring about the blissful arising of mantra-siddhi.
One should draw mandalas and the like, and have images of the Buddhas fashioned;
the best of divine substances and liquors, when being prepared by the gods,
are accomplished by practitioners of mantra when joined with the proper constellations and sages.
When a human is born from a *mithuna* (a pair),
then listen to the signs of their destiny and the time of their attainment of perfection (*siddhi*).
One is born wealthy, industrious-minded, yet deceitful and foolish;
if one is renowned while situated therein, it is like the stars adorning the night sky.
Then, that mortal becomes beloved by his kin, always dear to them, wealthy, endowed with resourcefulness, and is known as a great lord.
With the remaining malefic planets and various other contemptible ones,
one is born as a rogue, afflicted by passion and overwhelmed by diseases.

Indeed, his mantras—whether for pacification (*śāntika*) or supreme nourishment (*pauṣṭika*)—will not succeed; nor will those for minor rites, nor those that cause dejection. Furthermore, there will always be the sight of carnivorous and flesh-eating beings, as well as cruel and preeminent planets.
For the sake of accomplishing these mantras, one should employ them in cruel rites;
however, going there is forbidden, with the exception of the foremost five.
In all rites there, success in going and coming is not achieved;
likewise, for those [rites], one should bestow minor rites, knowing them in every respect.
Those two chief planets known as white are auspicious; the other two are sinful.
Seeing four of the chief planets is the source of prosperity.
Both Mars and Saturn are red and black; this is the appearance of those who perform cruel deeds.
Mercury and Jupiter are white, like the bright moon, while Venus and Rāhu are yellow.
Arka and Aṅgāraka are both red, born of the earth, and situated in the [southern] direction; Ṣaṇḍa and Rāhu are likewise black; the remaining planets are variegated.
They are said to be possessed by various grahas, diverse and beautifully adorned with their constituent elements;
some have various forms, while others are intent upon various weapons.
Presided over by various groups of elemental spirits, and taught by various ancient seers,
all the planets are attended by apsarases and kinnaras.

Abiding in the sky, they have attained their state through their color; they are known by their modes of movement and origins; all of them move through the intermediate space, traveling together with the constellations.
Having arrived in the sky by means of flight, she possessed various modes of movement and activity;
through her power, she was endowed with great supernatural faculties, both in her gait and in her form and attire.
These have been taught by all the best of sages, joined with the true meaning of ritual action;
they are to be employed on the fourth day and applied to the four types of beings.
Four excellent planets are proclaimed: the white and the yellow ones accomplish one's goals;
the remaining ones are employed in cruel rites, as are the red and the black ones.
One should not perform any rites, especially those for pacification,
when these two planets are black or red, nor on the fourteenth lunar day.
One should not perform all types of activities; one should accomplish minor tasks.
A seeker of wealth should accomplish auspicious undertakings during the period of Mānuṣa Gaṇanā.
The wise one should always have a seat, a bed, and a temple constructed quickly by those very [artisans]; he should cause all difficult passages to be cleared.
A person born under the sign of Cancer is seen to be auspicious;
he may quickly become a teacher or a universal monarch (cakravartin).
O venerable ones, let there arise for these living beings an awakening produced by their past karma, as well as the vision of the Moon, Indra, the Planets, and the other principal deities.
On an auspicious day and in an auspicious place, the Bodhisattva was born;
joined with the Puṣya constellation, those honored by the gods were born.
The Buddhas, the teachers of the three worlds, as well as others of great supernatural power,
are kings, rulers, and sovereigns of many living beings.
In this world, various types of people are born, marked by the planets Śani, Arka, and Aṅgāraka; some are mortals who abound in progeny and are devoted to their duties.
Those born under Puṣya are always born with various modes of conduct;
therefore, know that the fruit of karma is the destiny resulting from one's own actions.
But those who follow right conduct, when engaged in the rites of the planets, teach them here in such a way that they do not depend on worldly dharmas, just as the Jinas have taught.
Karma is the cause of the world's diversity; it arises from the meditative absorption of the world-system.
It is the vessel for all worlds, the source from which their names and supports arise.
O gods, best of beings, understand that which has been told in the world as manifold;
for even in the past, the affectionate one recounted that which is born of karma.
Then the wise Bodhisattva Mañjughoṣa, possessing great supernatural power and common to all beings, made this request out of a desire for the welfare of sentient beings.
Everything born of karma has been explained in detail through the mantras and tantras;
O all you gods, this is indeed the single Dharma that is always [to be followed] by you.
To one born under the sign of Cancer, he should give a mantra for nourishment;
thereafter, the sign of Leo appears to the man.
A mortal born under Siṃha will indeed be a hunter of sheep;
he will be deceitful toward women, a consumer of meat, and a dweller in mountain caves.
Likewise, the protector of the earth,
acting as the great overseer, should always cause the earth to be governed by a commander-in-chief who is both fierce in action and ever pure.
He was ungrateful, a breaker of his word, constantly devoted to evil deeds,
a betrayer of friends, ever greedy, and likewise deceitful.
If it is always aspected by wise planets that are white or yellow, one born there becomes righteous; if by those that are black, he is considered deceitful.
Therein, the rite for prosperity (pauṣṭika) has been fully taught for those desiring success;
it also brings about rising into the sky, moving through the air, and the attainment of supreme pride.
One should avoid any other accumulated karma that is similar;
beyond that, the sign of Leo is known as the constellation Kanyā.
Born there, one becomes a rogue, a thief, a miser, and a deceiver;
always lustful toward women, greedy, cruel, and perpetually impulsive.
He is foolish, an adulterer, stubborn, and always puffed up with pride;
yet, he is born under an auspicious lunar mansion and weekday, with the rising of planets in favorable aspects.
Those seen by planets that are yellow or white are born very wealthy;
they possess pure mantras, are always wise, and abide in pure conduct.
One should accomplish on the surface of the earth those mantra-tantras that have arisen,
which quickly bring about one's goals and those which are proclaimed for the sake of nourishment.
The knower of mantras shall accomplish all [rites] belonging to the families of the limbs of the Jinas,
as well as those mantras headed by the Lord of Jinas that have been proclaimed in many ways.
The knower of mantras shall accomplish all things within the signs and their respective classes;
beyond that, there is the sign celebrated by the name Tula.

One should not frequent that [place] which is well-known, abounds in ritual activity, and is dependent upon it; for the wise person, when engaged in the attainments of mantra, is born equal to the scales.
One should not perform any ritual practice that arises from attachment to the earth; for the sake of accomplishing all mantras, one should act within the various states of existence and wombs.
One born under the sign situated in Libra is always seen to be deceitful, miserable, greedy, and envious, and is constantly devoted to the scales.
The practitioner of mantra, having resorted to that lunar mansion, should always perform it—
that which the world does not declare to be the ground for the attainment of wealth and prosperity.
When one is born under the chief of the planets (the Sun) at that time, surrounded on all sides by yellow and white [planets],
one shall not attain success in mantra, even with effort for the sake of protecting wealth and prosperity.
When all this is being accomplished in a mere moment by those who are appointed,
and when it is observed on all sides by auspicious planets that are yellow and white;
A great-souled, heroic, and righteous lord of men is born when one is aspected by extremely cruel planets, such as Saturn, the Sun, Mars, or those born from Leo.
If the meaning of the natal ascendant falls on Libra, the man becomes envious,
suffers from many diseases, is poor, and experiences the arising of afflictions caused by illness and disease.
One who is fierce in all actions, cruel, and always impulsive should not engage in rites for pacification as spoken by the Lord in the essence of the Jina’s teachings.
He performs fierce deeds arising from the assembly for the wielder of the thunderbolt,
as well as rites of sorcery and various acts of war.
In that heap, always in that family and born from that [lineage],
even a despicable action attains success there through the supreme Victors.
One should avoid the expansion of primary qualities and powers,
and one should not undertake travel to foreign lands in the direction of Māśuja.

One should not perform any rites involving Mount Mandara as a vehicle, nor anything concerning the conditioned or unconditioned realm of sentient beings, while the Sun is in that [twelfth] zodiacal sign.
When [the fetus] emerges from the scorpion, it takes refuge in the womb of a sentient being;
listen now as the various signs that arise are described.
Such a person is born on the surface of the earth as one who is fierce, reckless, cruel, difficult to overcome, arrogant with pride, crooked, and greedy.
A mortal shall be wise, righteous, learned, yet crooked and difficult to approach;
he shall be beloved by women, grateful, and firm in his prowess.
Constantly engaged in the practice of tantra and mantra, devoted to service, and worshipping the guru;
the appearance of the chief planets—Venus, the Moon, Mercury, and Jupiter—is auspicious.
It is praiseworthy, conducive to the highest good, the goal to be attained, and an increaser of longevity and health;
it is for the purpose of accomplishing the vision of those [deities] during the higher practice of the mantra-practitioners.
When Saturn, the Sun, Mars, or Rāhu aspects that man,
he becomes cruel, impulsive, perverse, and a performer of fierce deeds.
And for those practitioners of cruel deeds, the mantras of Vajrin will be accomplished;
no mortal shall come from any quarter during even the most despised days.
Beyond that, mortals are born in many ways according to their destination and location within the zodiacal sign called Dhanus, as taught by the Tathāgatas.
And all were beautiful in their youth, though they shared in suffering;
thus have the designations of their respective lifespans been proclaimed.
Likewise, I shall declare the accomplishment of wealth and the attainment of prosperity;
[such speech] would constantly destroy one's own source and cause the source of another to increase.
A mortal born under the sign of Sagittarius (Dhanu) will have many wives, be talkative, be fond of various passions and pleasures, and remain unrestrained.
If there is the aspect of the principal planets that are white or yellow, one is born as a lordly, illustrious, ever-competent, and even righteous person.
One should practice their mantras, which arise from various weapons,
or which bear the fruits of various arms, as well as those pertaining to garments, ornaments, and vehicles.
Indeed, his mantras— arising from the limbs favored by the Munis and produced from various elements as well as from the results of those various elements— will surely attain success.
Thereafter, the mantra-practitioner should have all rites performed with all ritual substances; thus he shall produce, in every respect, a state of rebirth that is free from calamity.
One's own home, vehicle, daughter, and residence,
as well as all desired things, great wealth, and the state of ascending upward.
For his success, the liberated soul quickly stands in his hand;
thereafter, in the sign of Capricorn, he is seen as equal to the highest heap.
A mortal born among them may always recognize [them] by these signs:
he is devoted to his mother, devoted to his father, renowned, highly esteemed, and a master.
Though wealthy and a collector of riches, he was born thus: unable to endure any suffering, miserly, greedy-minded, and deceitful.
For those [planets] aspected by Venus and Jupiter, all prosperity arises;
however, those which are black or red planets result in cruel actions, as previously described.
The knower of mantras should not go there from any direction or intermediate point;
he should accomplish malevolent rites and avoid those that are undesirable.
One should set out on a voyage toward the northern direction;
one should embark upon a ship for the purpose of reaching the great ocean and obtaining wealth.
Therein, one may obtain prosperity arising from the region presided over by the sign of Pisces;
beyond that, it is called "Kumbha," following the emergence from Capricorn.
Those born under the sign of Aquarius are always said to have their nature based on living beings;
they are described by the best of men as being of many kinds and possessing many characteristics.
Variegated and of diverse forms, yet by virtue of their reliance on caste and birth,
these men are born dark-complexioned, large-eyed, and highly esteemed.

Those born in the zodiac sign of Aquarius (Kumbha) are said to be incapable of sexual desire, yet they contemplate matters of worldly pleasure and wealth; they are grateful and righteous, and are born of mantras.
In this world, planets that are white or yellow are seen and highly honored;
however, those planets that are black or red arise from the manifestation of their innate nature as they are perceived.
Such men are always born with missing limbs, wretched, foolish, fickle, prone to theft, afflicted by many diseases, and impoverished.
One should not have them perform the supreme rite honored by the sages,
by which [the deities] born from the limbs of Aṅga might grant [their favor] in all rites.
One should not go even after reaching the edge of the shore; therefore, this has not been described at all.
One should perform the rites of the Vajra family with the desire to attain the accomplishment of mantra.
One should accomplish here the mantra that is fierce, ending with a cruel action, adorned with the syllables *sphaṭ* and *huṃ*, and properly joined with the King of Wrath;
even those of sinful deeds succeed when applied to these rites of a terrible nature.
Beyond that, the Tathāgatas have declared the sign of Pisces;
all the young men situated there are seen to possess many sectarian marks.
These are the characteristics arising from those born in the sign of Pisces:
he is a lord, possessed of honor and intelligence, illustrious, endowed with a hundredfold abundance of enjoyments,
and he becomes a sovereign over all the worlds upon this earth.
Then a wise king was born who swiftly accomplished his aims;
born from the sight of the moon-like Śukra, he became the best of men in the world.
From the sight of wise and long-lived persons, one becomes wealthy;
moreover, possessing a tall stature and large eyes, he shall always be beloved by women.
A ruler of men who has many enemies becomes crooked;
whereas one who has many friends is born as Śukra, being affectionate toward his friends.
Beyond that, if the cruel Divākara, the chief of planets,
looks upon mortals, as do Śani, Rāhu, and Bhauma;
Then the banner becomes "suffering" and indeed "cruel";
for these planets have been described as before during both the dark and the bright fortnights.
One should perform all rites while resting in the zodiac sign of Pisces;
when the moon is situated therein, one should observe it and accomplish everything.
Beyond this, there are the hosts of elephants, humans, and non-humans,
as well as Gandharvas, Rākṣasas, Garuḍas, and Pannagas.
Their mental manifestation, characterized by their own nature, genus, destiny, and location, should be recognized by these very signs.
Just as the nature of a being is, so is their *liṅga* explained;
for these [beings] have their own mantras spoken, and one should employ those very [mantras] for them.
In the world, the zodiac signs are said to be exactly twelve, born from the Gaṇas;
they are calculated by the foremost of the planets and joined with the lunar mansions.

These have indeed been described in brief, for they would be too extensive to relate in full; at that time, [the Buddha] established them for human beings according to the lunar mansions and the circles of planets.
But beyond this, the knowledge of the gods and the sages of great supernatural power proceeds; that which occurs therein is the conduct of humans.
The knower of all mantras should accomplish the inconceivable vision of wisdom regarding the qualities of the Buddhas, which arises from the most excellent of birth-signs.

One should always practice on the lunar days (tithis) associated with one's own constellation during the bright fortnight; success is always proclaimed to be found in these, while for those engaged in dark rites, it is in the dark fortnight.
One should perform [the rites] during the days when the planets are white or yellow;
one should employ [these] on the full moon days occurring during the bright fortnight.
One should cause [the disciple] to choose on the third day of the bright fortnight of the month of Prajāpati,
or on the fifth, the seventh, or the tenth and eleventh days.
Likewise, on the thirteenth day of the bright fortnight, one should perform all rites:
for the sake of nourishment, the yoga of pacification, and auspicious or inauspicious travel and arrival.
One who abides in the mantras and tantras should always take delight in dance and song; furthermore, the wise one should attend to ornaments, vehicles, dwellings, and the art of shaving.
When employed by wise and illustrious mortals in every way,
it grants the constant attainment of enjoyments, wealth, and the meeting with beloved beings.
The foremost sages have taught that various rites are performed for different purposes;
therefore, those who possess wealth and seek prosperity should swiftly accomplish the realization of the mantras' purpose.
By the Moon, Venus, Jupiter, and Mercury—
the most excellent of divine planets, well-honored, pure, and auspicious.
One should always meditate upon the mantras associated with the lunar days (tithis), as well as those indicated in brief by the fierce and terrible-formed planets and the lunar days themselves.
One should perform fierce rites during the dark fortnight for those who perform black deeds,
as well as the summary of the destination and place [of rebirth], and the application of mantras for the accomplishment of their purpose.
The planets, the meanings of the zodiac signs, the lunar mansions, and the lunar days are fully explained here,
along with the power of the accomplishment of rites and the rules for all ritual actions.
Thus ends the third chapter on the knowledge of astrology from the seventeenth detailed section of the *Āryamañjuśrīmūlakalpa*, an extensive Mahāyāna sūtra belonging to the *Bodhisattvapiṭaka*.
Now begins the twentieth detailed section.
Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, having again gazed upon the abode of the Pure Abodes, addressed Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta:

Mañjuśrī, in the extensive ritual manual (*kalpavisara*) of your [teachings], there are described marvelous signs and marks that dispel the causes for the arising of all fears. These indicate auspiciousness and inauspiciousness, as well as abundance or famine, invasion by foreign armies, drought, or excessive rain; they also foretell obstacles for sentient beings during great ritual accomplishments (*mahāsādhana*) and the like. Therefore, the practitioner must reflect upon them and discern what is achievable or unachievable, and what should or should not be done in that particular region.
Therefore, if the signs are not auspicious, one should depart from that place and go elsewhere to perform the rites;
however, if the signs are auspicious,
they should be performed in that very same place.
And one must remain right there.

Having understood this, the practitioner devoted to the practice of mantra must determine what is to be done and what is not to be done; having recognized the signs within the practice of mantra, one must discern what is auspicious and what is inauspicious.

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, having prostrated at the feet of the Blessed One, spoke again as follows: "It would be well, O Blessed One, if you would teach the detailed exposition of the chapter on the knowledge of omens (*nimittajñāna*).

That will be for the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings, and for the sake of those bodhisattva mahāsattvas engaged in the practice of mantras, regarding the signs and marks that arise from the results of both auspicious and inauspicious [actions].

By means of this, all those sentient beings who have entered the practice of mantras, having known whether a task is achievable or unachievable and the timing of the omens, shall know when they should remain and when they should depart."
When this had been said, the Blessed One Śākyamuni addressed Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta:
"Therefore, Mañjuśrī, listen and pay close and careful attention; I shall speak to you."
First of all, there will appear the omen consisting of the simultaneous arising of portents:
a great terror, unprecedented, and the activity of non-human beings.
And all the planets and constellations, the kūṣmāṇḍas, the graha-rākṣasas,
the mātṛs, the deities, and all the pretas of great supernatural power.
Then, when great portents occur, they display a sign that is first auspicious,
then middling, and finally inauspicious.
Understand that among all human beings on this earth, they declare various causes for the destruction of one's standing on the ground.
Headless trunks and various kinds of birds are seen everywhere in the world; therefore, one should depart from that region.
At night, having seen Indra’s weapon, especially the bow, as well as arrows,
iron shafts, nooses, and various other weapons arising from the sky,
one should depart from that place.
When deformed shapes such as headless trunks and puppets are seen dancing in the sky within the lunar orb,
they say that a hollow or a cavity is visible within the circle of the moon.
If men of high and low status should be seen fighting within the lunar orb in the world of mortals, one should depart from that place.
Various life-taking beings and diverse hosts of spirits may also fight while dancing; therefore, one should depart from that place.
Residing within the visible sphere, one sees a lunar disc resembling the shape of a mandala;
having seen such a thing, one should depart from that place.
If all the constellations are seen fighting within the lunar disc,
then whichever one among them falls first, that is said to be the "direction of the gods" (devadik) belonging to whichever [king] it occupies; that king will certainly die.
Having seen such a being, which arises in various forms,
one should quickly depart from that place out of fear before long.
And Śara, Nārāca, and Śakti, seeing there in the night-maker (the moon) the harassment caused by thieves and the imminent fear arising from the falling of weapons, [acted].
Having seen beings of deformed appearance taking refuge in various creatures upon the earth at night under the moon, one should therefore depart from that place.
The birds are black, white, yellowish-white, red, and likewise smoky; their forms are naturally deformed.
When those people on the surface of the earth are seen to have become discolored,
having observed such a sign, one should depart from that region.
The bright fortnight may become dark, and likewise the dark fortnight may become bright;
moreover, birds on the surface of the earth appear with distorted forms.
Having observed such omens, one should therefore depart from that region.
Herds of deer and jackals, wild beasts, serpents, rogues, barbarians, oppressors, and thieves— all these would enter the village and its dwellings.
For them, there may arise fear-induced famine, as it has been described,
and various hosts of spirits will also be seen upon the surface of the earth.
Yakṣas, rākṣasas, and kinnaras, possessing both deformed and unaltered forms,
constantly dance upon the surface of the earth by day and by night;
having seen such a sign, one should therefore depart from that region.
Men, women, and youths shall weep bitterly upon the ground;
likewise, there will be constant illness there day and night, and the arrival of calamities.
Ugliness and repulsiveness are seen among serpents upon the surface of the earth—
in houses, on roads, in temples, and near trees;
they remain pervading everywhere, and there shall be great fear.
There will be the calamity of a great plague, the fainting caused by poisons and boils,
famine, and the destruction of the kingdom when people gather there.
When birds, dogs, and jackals— with hideous, deformed,
and loathsome muzzles— raise their beaks and howl in the sky with distorted faces;
At midnight and at midday, both times are contemptible for mortals;
there will quickly arise great fear and the arrival of a foreign army.
In brief, there will be famine and excessive rain;
for one month and seven days, they shall be tormented by great suffering.
Human beings dwelling upon the earth will become mutual thieves and be consumed by fire;
there will be great fear of weapons in that place, and therefore one should depart from that country.
Clouds arising in curved shapes are seen everywhere in the sky;
they are clearly defined, fierce, and resound with intense thundering.
Seven distinct [planets] are seen as resting upon the serpents, while two or four are seen as resting upon the sky— extremely terrible and possessing fearsome faces.
Upon seeing such a sign, there will immediately arise great fear therein,
as well as the calamity of a great pestilence, fever, disease, and indeed most terrifying ailments.
Then the stationary and moving poisons that swiftly take life will be released;
then the clouds will discharge a terrible rain.
There, the beings perish, being mutually indifferent to one another;
having observed such a characteristic, one should therefore depart from that place.
I shall describe to you the great famine of the great precipice, the falling of meteors on all sides, the comets, the thunderclaps, and the conflagrations of the quarters.
Listen: a fall from a precipice situated within sight occurs, as does the appearance of meteors;
if a fall of meteors should take place on all sides, both by night and by day, the practitioner of mantra, recognizing this as a great danger and ill-health, should depart from that place.
One should always go toward the direction where a great meteor is blazing;
such is the defeat of kings, for fear comes from whatever direction the face [of the omen] is turned.
When a meteor falls in all directions throughout the night at all times,
there shall be a great plague in that region, as well as famine and the destruction of the king.
When meteors fall on all sides by day or by night,
such shall be the death of kings and ministers;
having perceived this, one should practice the recitation of mantras, and knowing this, one should depart from that country.
If a comet falls from battle, there is danger from whichever direction its tail points;
or else, some other defeat of kings is seen in the thick of the fray.
Then, when great meteors fall everywhere swiftly upon that land marked by planetary signs, he shall cause a great upheaval; therefore, one should depart from that region.
In whichever direction a meteor, having entered [the sky], constantly falls from its station,
in that direction disease, famine, and the ruin of the kingdom shall arise.
Death occurs for the stars during their departure and arrival because they depend upon them;
whoever is born under a lunar mansion (nakṣatra) shall experience the fear of death from that very source.
Within two nights a living being perishes, and within a nakṣatra [time] one falls to the earth;
this same rule shall apply to all sovereigns of men.
If this deity is seen as agitated by the desired [object],
then one should know that there is certainly fear of death for him within six months; this is taught regarding the vision at night, whereas during the day it concerns the image.
If the image of a person's chosen deity should move,
laugh, or weep, one should always avoid that place.
The image indeed falls or shatters by its own accord;
its destruction occurs swiftly, O lord of men, as do his houses,
while they fashion various kinds of lingas of diverse forms.
If a statue is seen situated in a temple or a sanctuary,
having seen such a thing, one should depart from that place.
The mantra practitioner should always see the image from all sides and everywhere as having a deformed and loathsome appearance, assuming various kinds of distortions.
Whether the mantra-practitioner sees it himself or others on earth,
having observed such a characteristic, he should depart from that place.
If it is seen at midnight or during the third watch of the night, there will be a great rain of stars; therefore, one should depart from that region.
Likewise, during the fourth part of the night, the stars move swiftly;
they go toward that region like fireflies, so one should not frequent it from any side.
One should then go to that place where they travel along the surface of the earth;
one should go there where rain is doubted and where the stars move.
One should not quickly enter that region where there is great fear from rain;
that region will swiftly perish through the arrival of a foreign army.
One should know that country to be agitated by famine, the falling of weapons,
thieves, serpents, beasts of prey, barbarians, and rogues.
A king whose kingdom has been lost and who has taken refuge from an enemy force should constantly dwell in that region, moving in every direction.
After eight years and one month, they shall regain that country;
then he shall obtain the kingdom and return once more from that land.
Having understood all modification as being joined with action through its initial onset,
the reciter should always commence that [practice] at the proper time for action in brief.
If great meteors are seen falling mixed together constantly from all sides, one should depart from that region.
Many forms of fire are seen with various bases;
there are yakṣiṇīs of diverse kinds, possessing wonderful forms and great supernatural powers.
From the two regions of its mouth, it emits blazing flesh-eaters and female piśācas;
therefore, one should examine the meteor by means of these aforementioned signs.
They are proclaimed to be very long, short, or of medium length;
they may measure four cubits, two cubits, or even just one cubit.
They are seen on the surface of the earth by mortals; they take recourse in great prosperity, possess great vital power, and are of sublime form—this deity is possessed of great supernatural might.
And those inhabitants of heaven, summoned with forms of various appearances,
were present when that great and terrifying battle between the gods and asuras was taking place.
"I command Śakra: go quickly here to that earth below, to the mortals dwelling in Jambūdvīpa—the men, the yakṣas, and the lords of men."
They behold all the worlds and investigate what is dharma and what is adharma;
they are respectful toward their mothers, devoted to their fathers, and those who honor their elders in the family.
When all the men dwelling in Jambudvīpa become holders of the great mantras and practitioners of recitation,
then the gods experience great festivals and the Daityas suffer defeat.
The mortals dwelling in Jambudvīpa were then most righteous;
at that time, Vāsava, the lord of the thirty-three gods, possessed great energy.
Then the Asuras, their enthusiasm shattered and their minds broken,
took refuge in pride, by which they entered Pātāla.
As they entered their own city there, their pride shattered and their pain assuaged,
the gods, the lords of the thirty-three, then attained great joy.
Then, throughout Jambudvīpa, people everywhere enjoyed abundant food and good health;
men and women, freed from all suffering, moved about in every direction at ease.
Therefore, O people, you should in every way cultivate devotion toward the Buddha,
toward the Dharma, and toward the vast Saṅgha, which has transcended dualities and is free from affliction.
"O mortals, perform worship if you desire to obtain all prosperity.
Then he performed the practice of mantra, and auspicious speech arose from him.
Perform the ten deeds as they are established in the world— leading to the higher realms and free from rebirth— as a gathering of people, with minds purified in three ways.
One should always abstain from killing living beings, nor should one take what is not given; one should not consort with another's wife, avoiding those women who are forbidden;
and one should recite [mantras].
Be content with your own duty; take care, O best of people!
One should not speak falsehood, for its ripening is nothing but suffering.
One should not speak harsh words that cause suffering for the sake of all sentient beings,
nor any speech whatsoever that is associated with afflictions or devoid of meaningful purpose.
One should never practice speech that is empty, though joined with the meaning of the Dharma, nor that which is divisive; one should always avoid slander and words that cause dissension among others.
The preeminent sages have forbidden any action with a defiled mind; one should not perform the act of covetousness toward those beings who are helpful to others.
One who would never perform for another that which arises from hatred should abandon the karma of malice, which finds no footing in the hearts of sentient beings.
People should not cause harm to other beings in any way,
nor should they entertain wrong views, which destroy all wholesome qualities.
There is no giving and no offering, nor is there any success in the practice of mantras;
likewise, the mantras conceived according to the meaning of all tantras do not achieve accomplishment.
For the Buddhas, there is no arising of pleasure, nor is a quiescent nirvāṇa desired;
nor is there such practice or awakening as that which occurs through the attainment of individual objects.
Arhatship does not arise in this world nor among phenomena;
such is the diverse nature of things in the world, according to their respective meanings and realities.
A practitioner of mantra should never associate with such women— many of them, marked by various signs— as they give rise to sinful views.
The ten actions, as they have been described, when practiced with abstinence, are traditionally held to lead to heaven;
their cultivation indeed results in the attainment of Nirvana, which is the source of all welfare.
Then, an undesirable defeat of the gods in the world occurred,
and the pride of the Daityas increased, arising from their excessive arrogance and wealth.
Then, in the abode of people, all the inhabitants of Jambūdvīpa were quickly afflicted by diseases, and they also fainted one after another.
Then all those overseers of people, having committed offenses against one another and being devoid of the dharma and purpose of the sages, will all quickly perish.
In that battle, for those whose minds were filled with rage, death came through the clash of weapons;
yet they did not seek refuge even with the foremost of the gods, who stood threatening them in that place of no shelter.
Those kings, being impure, did not worship the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha;
nor did they quickly recite mantras; those kings remained always in that state.
Then the worlds, overwhelmed by various miseries, began to perish;
thereupon those foremost Daityas, quickly and with great fury, ascended it.
The best of men enter the summit of Mount Sumeru;
at that time, the auspicious terraces of Meru divide into mansions.
Mounted upon various excellent chariots and adorned with diverse ornaments, they cause the forest to be completely destroyed on all sides for the sake of the denizens of heaven.
Wielding various weapons, they offered the foremost victory;
then they approached Khara, who took hold of the Apsarases.
All those lords and powerful asuras, arrogant in their strength,
seized a celestial maiden, as well as the nectar and the food.
Then those most excellent of the best gods entered that supreme city;
having gone to the summit of Mount Meru, they beheld the city that is the refuge of all vision.
All the Piśācas, followed by Śakra, indeed entered that most excellent city-gate; yet Māyā, the mother of the city, did not succumb to fear, but took refuge in joy.
Having turned back from there, all those gods went to their own abodes;
for when the singular accomplishment of the mantra has been attained, one should dwell in the refuge of Janayum.
Even a mortal who has recited the mantra, while dwelling in that abode,
will find that in that land there are no afflictions, no famine, and no enemies.
When this earth is protected by one who has mastered the recited mantra, neither disease nor fear shall exist;
nor indeed will any bandits be able to cause harm here.
There, neither distress nor death occurs, nor do transgressions of bounds; there is no pain, no fainting from disease, and it removes the affliction of fever and illness.
When those who have recited the mantra take refuge in it, they are not afraid on that earth;
for these excellent mantras spoken here originate from the family of the Lord of Jinas.
Likewise, the lotus-born mantras, when honored with mantras by the practitioner,
[bestow] there that supreme mantra which possesses great supernatural power, comparable to Jahnu.
Then those most excellent of the foremost gods [will prevail], while the defeat of the asuras occurs;
for when will such virtues as these ever be seen here upon the surface of the earth?
On this earth, logicians of various forms proclaim through their tradition that "this is a planet," for the sake of elaborating upon the purpose of its descent.
The knowledge of meteors has been sung by the best of sages and indicated therein by the signs of the planets; now the description of their impact will be proclaimed.
When meteors fall and there is a thunderous crash upon the earth and its regions,
why is this roar of Pradyumna heard across the surface of the world?
They roared loudly toward that region, joined by these lunar days;
with a roar of incomparable sound, they even challenged that fierce one.
It is heard; roar quickly, for the voice of the great cloud is heard;
it is heard on the sixth, the fourth, the eighth, and also on the thirteenth day.
Likewise, during the dark fortnight, on the twelfth and fourteenth days,
when these are conjoined with these lunar mansions and the most excellent of the planets.
Understand that [the time] has passed during Aśvinī, Kṛttikā, and Bharaṇī,
as well as Pūrvabhādrapadā, and those joined with Ārdrā, Maghā, and Āśleṣā.
And when the planets— Saturn, the Sun, and Mars, being cruel— are well-honored [in their positions], yet they fall upon the earth;
A harsh sound that occurs when there is no rain or water is called *nighāta*;
in that region, there will indeed be great fear, famine, and the destruction of the kingdom.
One should know that there will be fear of foreign armies, various diseases, and great terror;
a thunderbolt shall fall upon the earth during these aforementioned asterisms.
Furthermore, when there are unfavorable planets that are black or red in color,
the king in that region is constantly and severely struck down by weapons.
At that time, in that fierce region, one should then recite the mantras;
at that time, various diseases and the loss of wealth are seen there.
In that case, there will be death, disease, and censurable famines;
one should predict a constant lack of rain for twelve years.
Resorting to the western direction, it falls from the sky onto the earth;
a thunderous crash, fraught with death, is seen by the thieves of death.
At that time, whether at midday or even when the sun has set,
one should likewise [worship] the rising, red-hued sun with auspicious sounds and disciples.
A contemptible sound at the three junctions of the day brings misfortune, whereas at other times it leads to satisfaction;
however, when the sound of a thunderclap occurs at midnight, there is great danger.
Let the best of kings have that excellent city made well-guarded there,
even though it is occupied by various groups of Mlecchas, rogues, and thieves.
When people on this earth act for the sake of benefiting the property of others during the final age, there will be an abundant sound of thunderous portents.
In that case, he shall become a chief minister; however, he will be afflicted by many diseases, and the king shall inflict upon him the state of being plagued by many ailments.
When that chief minister is slain, his wife is also killed;
all the toll-collectors there, who belong to various castes, are likewise destroyed.
Even those who serve the physician Jīvaka are slain by death;
so too are eminent merchants, chief officials, and kings appointed everywhere.
At that time, when the sun had reached the meridian,
those people who were like seers heard a thunderous and incomparable sound.
On this earth, she becomes everywhere afflicted by diseases;
otherwise, if men were to hear a tumultuous sound, [it would be as follows].

If a thunderous crash occurs suddenly and constantly from all directions, the king will not live there; however, if a favorable crash falls while resting upon the southern direction, it is auspicious.
If one hears thunder located in the eastern direction, one should predict that lightning and rain will follow shortly thereafter.
In that case, there will be a thunderous crash, and the governor of the eastern region will perish;
likewise, the people dwelling there who reside in the valleys of the Himalayan mountains [will be destroyed].
In that region, marked by a most terrifying eclipse, the superintendent of the people heard a sound: "The barbarians and thieves are being destroyed."
O child, the principal Vatsas and those inhabitants of various islands, as well as the sovereign of Nepal at that time, will be swiftly slain by their enemies.
In the intermediate directions there is Bhairava; in the sound (nāda) it is above and to the north.
Kāmarūpeśvara should always strike the ruler of Gauḍa.
Beyond the Lauhitya [river] dwell indeed the Jarādhyakṣas, the Jīvinas,
