Having gone down to a river that flows to the ocean and observed the fast for a fortnight while subsisting on milk and barley gruel, one should offer blooming white lotuses into the water.
One will see a treasure.

Having purified the body with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*), one who has performed the preliminary service (*puraścaraṇa*) from the first day of the bright fortnight until the full moon, having fasted for three nights at the conclusion, should take a thread spun by a young girl. Having bound it around the wrist after consecrating it ten thousand times before a reliquary stūpa (*sadhātuka-caitya*) or an image, one becomes invisible.
Having installed a cloth painting (*paṭa*) in a reliquary stūpa, one should offer thirty thousand lotuses.
Having kindled a fire with charcoal from *khadira* wood, one sees [the deity] in its own form.
Whatever one seeks, that one obtains,
beginning from the first day of the lunar fortnight up until the fifteenth.
Having fasted for three nights and performed a grand worship at a shrine containing relics, one should kindle a fire with *udumbara* wood and offer oblations of clarified butter.
One obtains a village.
One should cause a thousand stūpas to be constructed on the bank of a river flowing to the ocean;
having offered perfumes, flowers, incense, and so forth to each individual stūpa every day, one should have them consecrated eight thousand times with mantras.
When the western stūpa blazes,
then it should be known that the Blessed One is approaching with the Great Bodhisattva;
as he approaches, the earth trembles and fragrant scented winds blow.
One should recite [the mantra] until [the deity] stands before one in his own form;
whatever boon he requests, that he shall obtain.
One should offer eight thousand oblations of pieces of *khadira* wood leaves before the Blessed One.
He receives one dīnāra every day.
Having gone to the forest, subsisting on alms-food, he should offer twenty thousand oblations of wild cow-dung smeared with curd, honey, and ghee.
When the tree deity arrives, having assumed the form of a lion—
And he offers a pretext,
saying, "You must not accept it;
come to me yourself."
One should give a kingdom, wealth, or other jewels;
one must constantly provide enjoyments for the use of the Three Jewels.
Having retired to a forest, one should recite the mantra ten thousand times.
One should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times;
again, one should recite it one hundred thousand times.
In front of an image made of agalloch wood, one should offer seven thousand oblations of *vatsalaṇḍaka* seeds smeared with honey and ghee to the Blessed One.
The tawny wish-fulfilling cow (kāmadhenu) arrives.
If she does not arrive, one should again offer twenty thousand oblations of calf-dung.
Once she has arrived, she becomes perfected (siddhā).
He gives milk to a thousand men.
Before the cloth painting, one should offer eight thousand *jātī* flowers smeared with ghee and honey;
for six months, one obtains a thousand *dīnāras* or a thousand *paṇas*.
One should offer one hundred thousand blossoming lotuses smeared with curd, honey, and ghee into a reliquary containing relics; the deities who have faith in the Buddha will then grant boons.
Having performed worship to the noble Mañjuśrī, one should scatter white mustard seeds that have been consecrated seven times during a battle, and peace will prevail.

On the thirteenth day of the bright fortnight during the *pratihāraka* period, having performed worship with perfumes and flowers, one should offer eight thousand oblations of blooming lotuses smeared with ghee.
Then, taking the ashes and applying a tilaka mark on one's forehead, one should enter a village or city;
all [inhabitants] will become submissive.

Starting from the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight until the fifteenth, having fasted for one night, one should smear a mandala measuring four cubits beneath a tree, offer perfumes, flowers, and incense, perform worship to Noble Mañjuśrī, and present an offering to the yakṣas. Then, taking human bone, one should fashion a trident.
Having cast it with the left hand, one who has fasted for seven nights or three nights should offer eight thousand *jātī* flowers;
by that, the trident blazes.
Then one becomes accomplished;
whatever one creates by will, that one obtains.
[One obtains] a divine house at the time of an eclipse of the moon or sun, at a shrine containing relics, at an image, or in the house of a tawny cow.

Having taken a pala of cow's ghee from a cow that has a calf of the same age, and having placed it in a golden vessel, one should perform worship to the Blessed One; then, while not looking at the moon, one should recite the mantra until it fumes,
froths, and blazes.
By drinking it while it is steaming, one gains power over all sentient beings;
by drinking it while it is foaming, one becomes invisible;
by drinking it while it is blazing, one travels through the sky.

By performing the preliminary practice (*puraścaraṇa*) for six months, subsisting on cow’s urine and barley, observing a vow of silence, and reciting the mantra constantly, one obtains a hundred gold pieces without asking.

Starting from the fortnight of the *pratihāraka*, if one performs worship before the Blessed One, the noble Mañjuśrī, offering perfumes, flowers, and so forth, endowed with the eightfold *poṣadha* vows for one full year, one becomes accomplished;
the Blessed One performs the binding of the turban for such a person.
Having performed worship to Noble Mañjuśrī, beginning from the first lunar day until the full moon day, one should perform increasingly greater worship day by day;
monks should also be fed.
Then the words "I have attained success" will issue forth.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of clarified butter;
peace will come to another.

Having performed worship of the Blessed Buddha during the fortnight of miracles (prātihārakapakṣa), and having offered sublime perfumes, flowers, lamps, incense, and so forth to the noble Mañjuśrī, one should offer one hundred thousand *śaṅkhapuṣpī* flowers soaked in *iṅguda* oil.
There will be villages, cities, elephants, horses, chariots, cows, and buffaloes.

Having fasted for seven nights on a diet of milk and barley gruel, one who observes the *poṣadha* vow should fill a bowl with clarified butter strained [of impurities], light a lamp with a white wick, and show it to young boys and girls;
therein he will see the fulfillment of even limited knowledge.
There will be no fear from any calamities.
One who constantly recites the mantra should offer eight thousand oblations of clarified butter and fuel-sticks from the Bodhi tree.
Likewise, one should sleep before the cloth painting on a bed of *kuśa* grass.

In a dream, one sees twenty thousand pieces of wealth; a portion of this is to be applied to the Three Jewels. One should perform this before the cloth painting, beginning from the first day of the bright fortnight until the full moon.
In the meantime, one should recite [the mantra] eight thousand times day after day.

Having performed worship with perfumes, flowers, incense, and so forth, at the conclusion, having fasted for three nights and observed a vow of silence while reciting the mantra, one should place an offering (*bali*) in the hand of the attendants, go to a great highway, and announce the cruel spirit.
One should say, "Accept it."
Having taken a *droṇa* measure of white mustard seeds, one should scatter them toward the ten directions and below;
having empowered them twenty-one times with mantras, one should manifest oneself as supreme.
Likewise, on the eighth day of the dark fortnight, having entered the *gandhakuṭī*, one should recite the mantra a thousand times before the Blessed One.
Having performed the offering of oblations with incense, flowers, and so forth, one will then see the Blessed One, the Noble Mañjuśrī, in a dream.

During the month of Vaiśākha, in the dark fortnight, one who observes the *poṣadha* vows and subsists on a diet of milk and barley-gruel should perform worship at a reliquary (*caitya*) containing relics with incense, flowers, lamps, and other offerings. Furthermore, one should feed monks day after day, and four water-filled jars of "timely" roots should be placed there for the monks.

Having cast all medicinal seeds into [the fire], one should consecrate each one individually eight thousand times at night and place a son, a husband, or a daughter in a secluded place. For sovereignty:

having performed worship to the Blessed One and the noble Mañjuśrī on the eighth day of the dark fortnight within two weeks, one should kindle a fire in a cremation ground and offer eight thousand *śatapuṣpa* flowers as oblations.
Food and drink become inexhaustible.
Taking that very ash and applying it as a sectarian mark (*puṇḍraka*) on one's own forehead or that of another, if one enters into battle, all [enemies] will be brought under control;
one shall also be liberated from bondage and fetters.
It destroys [the obstacles] residing in fire.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of *mālatī* flowers smeared with curd, honey, and ghee,
while subsisting on cow urine for six months.
One obtains a thousand dīnāras.
Beginning from the first day of the bright fortnight, one should offer eight thousand blue lotuses;
he in whose name one offers them becomes submissive.
If one offers eight thousand oblations with the name of anyone during the three junctions of the five times, that person becomes submissive.
During the fortnight of miracles, subsisting on milk and barley gruel, one should recite [the mantra] three times daily before the cloth painting on the fifteenth day until the Blessed One arrives;
then the flame of the lamp will increase.
The earth trembles,
or the cloth moves,
or the words "it is accomplished" issue forth.
One obtains a thousand *dīnāras* and becomes a ruler of a province.

Having performed the preliminary practice (*puraścaraṇa*) for six months, one obtains five thousand *dīnāras* within six months before the Blessed One, the noble Mañjuśrī, at a shrine containing relics.
Having performed worship at a reliquary containing relics, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times;
one obtains a reward of one thousand gold pieces.
One should recite it one hundred thousand times at a reliquary containing relics.
He becomes a granter of all desires.
One who wishes to effect the pacification of all diseases should perform the consecration one hundred and eight thousand times; then, a thread spun by a maiden should be tied [around the wrist].
One obtains good fortune.
Illness will be pacified.
Having descended into a river that flows to the ocean, one should offer eight thousand black sesame seeds;
one will obtain wealth and grain.

At a shrine containing relics, beginning on the first day of the bright fortnight and fasting for three nights until the fifteenth day, one should kindle a fire with *udumbara* wood and offer one hundred thousand oblations of royal mustard seeds smeared with curd, honey, and ghee.
One will obtain five villages.
Kindling a fire with fuel-sticks of the *rājavṛkṣa*, one should offer one hundred thousand oblations of white sesame seeds smeared with curd, honey, and ghee.
If, having fasted for three nights on the fifteenth day, those sesame seeds go in every direction and intermediate direction, then one becomes accomplished;
one brings all sentient beings under control.
One should first recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times in the presence of the noble Mañjuśrī.
Then, during a lunar eclipse, having offered eight *palas* of ghee, one should recite it until it froths; by drinking this, one becomes a possessor of the power of memory (*śrutidhara*).
One should offer *kunduruka* incense one hundred thousand times.
One obtains one ancient [coin] that was not asked for.
If one offers eight hundred fragrant flowers every day before the noble Mañjuśrī,
one becomes possessed of glory.
One should offer eight thousand oblations daily of Apāmārga wood fuel sticks smeared with curd, honey, and ghee;
one will obtain a village.
Having kindled the fire with Bahuputrikā wood fuel sticks, one should offer eight thousand oblations of *vacā*.
One should make a tilaka mark with that ash; one becomes invisible.
If this does not happen, one should practice for a third time.
Having gone to the bank of a river during a lunar eclipse, one should kindle a fire with *bilva* wood and offer one hundred thousand oblations of *bilva* flowers smeared with ghee.
A yakṣa maiden comes.
Again, at midnight, having recited [the mantra] eight thousand times, one of them arrives;
whatever word is spoken, she performs it.

At the site of the treasure, one should recite the mantra eight thousand times after performing worship with flowers, incense, perfumes, and so forth; then, on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, having performed the offering of the bali, one should recite it.
The piśācas will arrive;
then one should dig.
The treasure-trove rises up;
having taken it, one should personally bestow it upon the Three Jewels.
The rite for the binding of the turban is likewise performed in this manner.
Having kindled a fire with *vibhītaka* wood in the presence of the Blessed One, one should offer eight thousand sesame seeds and rice grains every day;
a widow becomes submissive.
To subjugate a minister, one should offer white mustard seeds; he becomes submissive.
To bring a king under one's control, one should offer oblations of resin from the *sarja* tree;
he will become submissive.
To bring men and women under one's control, one should likewise offer oblations in this same manner.
Having kindled a fire with *agasti* wood, one obtains one hundred *dīnāras* before a cloth painting by means of lamp-wicks.
One should offer oblations of *palāśa* fuel-sticks while subsisting on a diet of milk,
three times each day.
One obtains a hundred gold pieces.
Having gone to a river that flows to the ocean, one should offer oblations a hundred thousand times;
one should accept whatever jewels one obtains.
A portion should be given for the use of the Three Jewels.
On the full moon day of Vaiśākha, one should recite [the mantra] throughout the entire night;
one will be liberated from the immediate transgressions (*ānantarya*).

Having performed worship of the Blessed One, Noble Mañjuśrī, at the foot of the Bodhi tree, one should offer oblations of *apāmārga* wood chips smeared with curd, honey, and ghee, dedicating it for oneself;
one will then be liberated from all sins.
Having consecrated seven grains of black pepper with mantras, one should consume them in a place free from crows;
one will then grasp five thousand verses and retain them for as long as one lives. Having performed one hundred thousand recitations before the Blessed Buddha, one effects the binding of serpents.
In water, one should offer a hundred thousand oblations of *vaikaṅkata* wood fuel sticks smeared with curd, honey, and ghee before the noble Mañjuśrī;
at midnight, one obtains five hundred *dīnāras*, half of which is to be dedicated to the Three Jewels.
One should offer eight thousand white water lilies day after day.
One becomes liberated from the Vināyakas.

During the bright fortnight of the month of Kārttika, subsisting on milk and barley-gruel or on vegetables, observing the poṣadha vows, and having fasted for three nights on the fifteenth day, one should offer a hundred thousand oblations of Vaikaṅkata fruits smeared with ghee. One obtains a thousand gold coins.
One becomes the lord of a village.
Half [of the merit] is for the use of the Three Jewels.

Having smeared a mandala the size of a cow-hide on a clean patch of ground, having constructed an altar in the shape of a lotus in its center, and having prepared an offering of various perfumes, flowers, incense, and bali-food, one should offer a hundred thousand oblations of fuel-sticks made of *vaikaṅkata* wood, each measuring a span of the Sugata.
Flames in the form of fire, blue in color, issue forth;
having circumambulated the practitioner to the right, they re-enter the fire-pit. In this way, one becomes accomplished.
In all ritual accomplishments (*sādhana*), fire must be invoked;
thus it becomes effective.
Having entered the water of the Gaṅgā up to one's shoulders, one should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times until the solar disc is seen in the sky.

Thereupon, the Blessed One becomes accomplished. If he does not see [the deity] and is not successful, he should go to a *ekavārāhī* (a one-nighter), perform the offering of perfumes, flowers, incense, and oblations, and recite the mantra for the entire night until dawn.
Then one becomes accomplished;
she should be invoked in all ritual practices,
and she will give me a hundred gold coins day after day.
Everything must be spent;
otherwise, he will not grant [the boon].
Having kindled a fire with *palāśa* wood, one should offer eight thousand oblations of wild cow-dung smeared with curd, honey, and ghee.
One obtains a hundred cows.
One should offer eight thousand *mātuluṅga* fruits into a fire of *palāśa* wood;
when Gaṇapati arrives, [the rite is complete].
He should be told: "Give me one dīnāra every day.
He gives it;
all of it must be spent.
He should be told, "Touch the feet of the Blessed One," and then he becomes successful.

Alternatively, one who has fasted for one night before a shrine containing relics or in front of a painting, having smeared *bilva* fruits with curd, honey, and ghee, should offer eight thousand oblations into a fire kindled with *vaikaṅkata* wood;
by this rite, he becomes glorious.
One becomes the sovereign of a region. One should offer *kiṅkirāṭa* flowers eight thousand times every day for seven days.
One obtains eight paṇas.
One who wishes to perform a rite for pacification should offer eight thousand oblations of parched grain;
peace will ensue.
One desiring nourishment should kindle a fire with fuel-sticks of milk-tree wood and offer eight thousand oblations of sesame seeds and rice at the three junctions of the day for three days; thus,
nourishment will come to pass.
Having kindled a fire with mango wood, one should offer eight thousand oblations of *dūrvā* sprouts;
in a dispute, one becomes the respondent.
At sunset, having taken the name [of the person], one should offer rice husks.
One should offer oblations with the left hand;
within seven nights, [the person] becomes submissive.
Having kindled the fire with *rāja* wood, one should offer eight thousand sesame seeds and rice grains at the three junctions of the day.
For three days, he bestows wealth.

In a pure place on the banks of the Gaṅgā, free from the sound of pestles, one should take earth from both riverbanks and construct a square altar seven cubits in size. Having fashioned a thousand-petaled lotus in the center and placed upon it a wheel made of the five red metals, measuring one span of the Sugata, one should perform the practice before the cloth painting in the middle of the maṇḍala. One should worship it with perfumes, flowers, and white sandalwood, offer a garland of mandārava and red flowers, and then perform worship with perfumes and other offerings. Seven rows of ghee lamps should be presented, and four jars of ghee should be ignited in the four directions.
In the four directions, four jars filled with all kinds of seeds and into which jewels have been cast should be placed.
Incense made of *kunduru*, *agaru*, *śrīpiṣṭaka*, and *guggulu* should be offered.
Having performed the ritual offering (*bali-vidhāna*), one should offer curd-rice and cakes in the four directions as previously described.
In the south, one should offer a mixture of water with cruel substances;
in the western direction, one should offer a vessel filled with milk and jaggery;
and in the northern direction, one should present an offering consisting of a vessel filled with milk-rice (*pāyasa*).
Then, having kindled a fire with *palāśa* fuel-sticks, one should offer eight thousand oblations of clarified butter over *apāmārga* fuel-sticks that have been consecrated seven times,
while uttering the name [of the person].
That person becomes submissive.

Having kindled a fire with *rājavṛkṣa* wood and fashioned an effigy out of salt, one should offer eight thousand oblations, beginning from the head down to the feet, taking the name [of the person] at each single oblation consecrated seven times;
thus the king becomes submissive.

On the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight, or on the eighth, having observed the *poṣadha* vows and fasted for a day and night, one should take unfallen cow dung and smear a sacrificial ground the size of a cow-hide. At a shrine containing relics, one should take fresh butter churned by a maiden from the milk of a tawny cow that has a calf of the same color, using either a silver vessel or one belonging to the noble Mañjuśrī. Seated upon a bundle of *kuśa* grass, holding the vessel with the left hand and stirring it with the ring finger of the right hand, one should recite the mantra until it becomes warm. That [butter] should be drunk;
one will then become possessed of great intelligence.
If it catches fire upon being spoken once, it brings about subjugation;
if it smokes, it brings about subjugation;
if it blazes, invisibility occurs.
One should offer eight thousand oblations of *bahuputrikā* wood.
With that ash, one should prepare four water-pitchers by mixing them together.
Having tied a mantra consecrated eight hundred times to one's right hand, one becomes a victorious debater in every instance.
One should offer eight thousand oblations of *aparājita* flowers;
one will remain undefeated in battle.
Knots should be made and tied with thread spun by a maiden that has been consecrated seven times;
neither stationary nor mobile poisons will prevail here.
For one bitten by a fierce serpent, taking the victim’s name, powdered water consecrated seven times should be given for drinking.
Even one who is dead rises up;
likewise, having consecrated it with mantras in the four directions, it should be given for drinking,
and even one bitten by Takṣaka lives.
One should smear the breast-ridge with clay consecrated seven times;
[the patient] is liberated,
and no pain occurs.

In the midst of a city during an outbreak of pestilence, having smeared a sacrificial ground at midnight and offered a white *bali* oblation, one should kindle a fire with fuel-sticks from milk-producing trees and offer a thousand oblations of milk;
this pacifies the pestilence.
If it is not pacified, [one should continue].
Then, on a certain day at the time of midday, having kindled a fire with *śleṣmātaka* wood, one should offer eight thousand oblations of white mustard seeds (*siddhārtha*).
This immediately pacifies pestilence.
When this rite is performed according to this method, all beings as many as there are become subject to his control.

For the subjugation of a *kūṣmāṇḍa*, one should offer eight thousand oblations of *kūṣmāṇḍa* wood; this pacifies an epidemic (*mārī*). For the subjugation of a *preta*, one should offer eight thousand oblations of sesame flour.
The pretas become submissive.
To subjugate piśācas, one should offer eight thousand oblations of rags from a cemetery;
the piśācas will become submissive.
For the subjugation of yakṣas, one should offer eight thousand oblations of fuel-sticks from the banyan tree (*vaṭa*) smeared with curd, honey, and ghee;
the yakṣas will become submissive.
For the subjugation of those possessed by epilepsy, jehāras, and the like, one should offer eight thousand oblations of wool-threads.
They become submissive.
One should offer eight thousand oblations of guggulu resin pills smeared with clarified butter;
the grahas who are followers of Mahādeva become submissive.
Having taken realgar purchased from a hero, one should kindle a fire with fuel-sticks of *arājavṛkṣa* wood and recite the mantra until it becomes the color of fire.
Then, having prepared fresh butter churned by a maiden from the milk of a tawny cow that has a calf of the same age, one should quench [the heated substance] in that clarified butter;
likewise in a vessel full of curd and in one full of honey.

Then, having performed protection by means of this very [mantra] and placed it in a casket, one who has fasted for three nights during a lunar eclipse should perform worship before the noble Mañjuśrī at a shrine containing relics. Placing it upon four leaves of the *aśvattha* tree while facing north, he should recite the mantra until it becomes warm, emits smoke, or blazes forth.
[The results are] subjugation, invisibility, and the power of traveling through the sky.
In the same way, one may use collyrium, yellow orpiment, and *rocanā*.

Regarding *rocanā*, this is the specific procedure: on the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight, having placed it upon a lotus leaf before the noble Mañjuśrī and holding it with cupped hands, one should recite the mantra until the threefold accomplishment is attained.
These rites are to be performed before the primary painting (*mūlapaṭa*).

Having fashioned a lotus out of the five metals for seven nights, one should grind saffron, rocanā, and camphor in water and smear the lotus with it. Then, on the eighth day of the bright fortnight, having observed the upoṣadha fast, bathed three times a day, and dressed in clean garments, one should stand before the image of Noble Mañjuśrī at a shrine containing relics. Holding [the lotus] with the right hand, one should recite the mantra until it blazes.
Then, by holding it, one becomes a vidyādhara and lives for ten thousand years.
Likewise, there are the bracelets, crowns, and chains.

In this manner, one should take equal portions of mountain-sandalwood, red sandalwood, guggulu, the root of *nandyāvarta*, the chaff of *girikarṇikā*, rice, *kuṣṭha*, *tagara*, honey, long pepper, and frankincense, and mix them together. Then, having taken the milk of a tawny cow that has a calf of the same color, and having kneaded it with butter churned by a maiden, one should form it into pills.
A lamp should be offered with unbroken sesame oil.

Then, having observed the *upoṣadha* fast and remained awake for a full day and night on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight, one should form pills by enclosing [the substance] within *aśvattha* leaves. One should recite the mantra before the noble Mañjuśrī until it emits smoke.
Having given some to one's companions, one should place [the remainder] in one's own mouth.
He becomes invisible;
then he blazes forth and becomes a traveler through the sky.
This is another method.

At a reliquary containing relics, before a cloth painting, one who observes the *poṣadha* vows should perform a grand worship, kindle a fire with *arka* wood fuel, and offer eight thousand oblations of *khadira* wood sticks smeared with curd, honey, and ghee. Beginning on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight until the fifteenth,
he becomes truly accomplished once [the rite] is completed.
In this manner, one who observes the *poṣadha* vows should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times;
thereafter, the ritual activities (*karmāṇi*) may be performed. Through this preliminary service (*pūrvasevā*), one becomes accomplished (*siddha*).

Now, if one desires to bring a king or a high official under one's control, one should perform worship to the Blessed One and offer eight thousand oblations of *rājavṛkṣa* wood fuel smeared with *iṅguda* oil,
beginning on the fourteenth day and continuing until the fifteenth.
By this ritual, success is achieved even for one of immoral conduct.
Desiring to bring the four castes under one's control, one should bring milk-rice (pāyasa), sacrificial food (haviṣyānna), and liquid gruel (peyā-kṛsara) and offer them as oblations;
they will become submissive.
At night, being pure, one should recite the mantra one hundred and eight times.
It liberates one from all bonds.
For the pacification of anger, one should perform a homa with rice husks; for the subjugation of a maiden, one should offer sesame seeds;
and for the desire of clothing, one should offer *karppaṇa*.
Having consecrated eight thousand stalks of *vacā* with eight thousand recitations over seven nights and binding them on one’s hand, whatever one asks for, that one obtains.
By constant recitation, if one binds with eight thousand consecrated lotus fibers (*padmasūtra*) or similar materials upon someone’s hand, protection is established for that person.
One desiring wealth should offer eight thousand oblations of balls of *guggulu* resin.
One who desires to become a head of a family (*kulapati*) should offer incense for seven nights; by offering it smeared with ghee for seven nights, one obtains a village.
If one gives flowers over which the mantra has been recited eight hundred times to someone, that person becomes submissive.

Saffron, *tagara*, *tālīśapatra*, lotus stalks, *śatapuṣpa*, and *śrīveṣṭa*—when these are combined and consecrated according to the ritual procedure, they serve as a means of subjugation for men and women when applied at a king’s gate, and they bring victory in battle. Having recited the mantra eight thousand times over a banner and having consecrated perfumes, flowers, and incense, one should offer an oblation (*arghya*) in seven vessels of curd;
by the mere sight of it, the enemy army shall perish.
Having consecrated black sesame seeds eight thousand times in front of the cloth painting, whoever eats them while pronouncing that person's name will become submissive.

Having recited [the mantra] eight thousand times over all seeds, all medicinal herbs, all fragrances, fragrant flowers, or lotuses, one should place them all in a jar of fresh ginger and recite it eight thousand times at the Bodhi tree;
or one may bathe oneself with them.
Or one may cause another to bathe;
that person becomes liberated from all calamities.
Or, if one offers oblations into smokeless embers with a lotus or a lotus leaf while reciting the name of someone, that person becomes submissive.
One should offer eight thousand oblations of bilva leaves mixed with honey;
this subjugates either the wife of a king or the queen.
For the subjugation of all beings, one should offer oblations of priyaṅgu.
If one offers red śāli rice while uttering the name of someone,
that person comes under one's control.
To subjugate a maiden, one should offer kesara flowers.
In front of the cloth painting (*paṭa*), one should offer eight thousand oblations of milk-rice (*pāyasa*).
By means of the name of whomever [one performs this], that person becomes submissive.

Having installed the cloth painting facing east at a shrine containing relics (*sadhātuka-caitya*), and having spread out a sacrificial altar (*vedi*) with *darbha* grass whose tips point toward the northeast starting from the first day of the bright fortnight, one should kindle a fire with *bilva* wood fuel and offer eight thousand blossoming lotuses smeared with curd, honey, and ghee during the three junctions of the day.
Incense made from agaru, turuṣka, kunduruka, and śrīpiṣṭaka should be offered.
One should present an offering of milk, curd, and cooked rice;
an offering for all spirits (sarvabhautika) should be given to the obstructors (vighnas).
Then, from the eighth day onwards, one should offer eight thousand oblations at the three junctions of the day using blossomed white lotuses smeared with curd, honey, and ghee;
one will obtain a great treasure or a kingdom.
One should offer eight thousand oblations every day using yellow flowers smeared with curd, honey, and ghee.
One obtains the desired place.
Having fasted for three nights, a fire sacrifice (homa) should be performed with a meal of barley meal;
in this way, success is achieved even for one who has committed the five acts of immediate retribution (ānantarya), provided [the rite is performed] seventy times one hundred thousand times.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of that very same kind, with fuel sticks smeared with curd, honey, and ghee;
one obtains ten million gold pieces.

Having risen early in the morning, being self-restrained and having bathed while observing celibacy, one who desires to bring under control a Nāgakeśara tree, a Priyaṅgu tree, a king, or a high official should offer eight thousand oblations after kindling the fire.
By performing this at the three junctions of the day, one obtains distinguished results within three months,
as well as abundant wealth.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of cow-calf dung;
one obtains a hundred cows.
With fuel-sticks of *priyaṅgu* and *nāgakesara*, for whomsoever one offers the oblation by name, that person becomes submissive.
One should offer eight thousand oblations of khadira wood fuel sticks smeared with curd, honey, and ghee before the cloth painting at the three junctions of the day;
one will obtain a great treasure.
That which is given becomes inexhaustible.
Having descended into a river flowing toward the ocean, one should cause a hundred thousand lotuses smeared with red sandalwood to float away;
one will see a treasure equal in size to that heap of lotuses.
One should offer eight thousand oblations of *bilva* fruits before the cloth painting at the three junctions of the day;
this produces enjoyments.
Having combined sesame seeds and rice grains, one should offer eight thousand oblations before the cloth painting at the three junctions of the day for seven nights.
Inexhaustible food arises.
One should offer *nāgapuṣpa* flowers to the *nāgas*;
they become submissive.
One should offer eight thousand pellets of guggulu incense before a yakṣa image for seven nights,
at the three junctions of the day, using fuel-sticks of aśoka wood;
the yakṣiṇī will then become submissive.
One should offer *śrīvāsaka* incense before the cloth painting;
the *kiṃnaras* will become submissive.
One who desires to bring the gods under control should offer eight thousand pieces of *agaru* wood fuel smeared with ghee before the original cloth painting, three times a day, for twenty-one nights.
They become submissive.
One should offer oblations of *kunduruka* resin before the cloth painting;
the *pretas* become submissive.
One should offer resin of the *sarja* tree;
the *vināyakas* become submissive.
By an oblation of oil-cake, one brings everyone under control.

Desiring to bring under one's control a king or a high official, one should offer eight thousand oblations of royal mustard seeds smeared with oil before the cloth painting for seven nights; they will become submissive.
Whatever one says, that he does.
To bring a princess under control, one should offer an oblation of black mustard seeds before the cloth painting.
Desiring to bring a royal priest under control, one should offer an oblation of clarified butter before the cloth painting.
For a Kṣatriya, one should offer oblations with armfuls of fuel; for the subjugation of a Vaiśya, one should offer milk;
for the subjugation of a Śūdra, one should offer kṛsarā.
For the subjugation of all women, one performs an oblation of salt;
for a widow, an oblation of mung beans;
and one brings all beings under control by offering them smeared with sesame oil.

For all [these], there is a fire sacrifice (*homa*) of eight thousand oblations for seven nights. Having become pure and having fasted for four meals, one should kindle the fire with *bilva* wood and offer *bilva* fruits into it.
One will see a treasure of a hundred thousand.
For twenty nights, subsisting on a diet of milk and barley-gruel, one should offer a hundred thousand oblations of white mustard seeds;
one will obtain wealth.
Having completed the preliminary practice (*puraścaraṇa*), one should offer oblations of yellow mustard seeds mixed with clarified butter before the cloth painting, day and night during the night.
Or, by fasting for four meals and offering this very same oblation ten thousand times for one month, wherever he desires, there shall be good rain;
he obtains wealth.
Having installed a cloth painting in a reliquary containing relics, and having kindled a fire with *palāśa* wood, one should offer a hundred thousand blue lotuses (*utpala*).
One obtains a village.
Alternatively, in front of the painting, while subsisting on a diet of milk and barley-gruel, one should offer lotuses (*padma*) along with perfumes, flowers, and incense.
One obtains a thousand gold pieces. If one performs a hundred thousand oblations before a cloth painting of Kumuda deities,
whatever one contemplates in the mind, that one obtains.
One should offer a thousand *bilva* fruits before the cloth painting;
one will see a treasure.
One who subsists on milk and barley gruel should offer one hundred thousand lotuses smeared with curd, honey, and ghee before the cloth painting.
One obtains a thousand pieces of gold.
Having fasted for three nights, one should offer eight thousand oblations of *agaru* (aloe) wood.
Then, a recitation (*jāpa*) must be performed throughout the entire night.
The cloth shakes,
or the garlands and wreaths move;
from that, one becomes accomplished.
Whatever one contemplates with the mind, that one bestows.
For the subjugation of a great person, one should offer *jātī* flowers before the painting.
For a difficult objective, one should offer *karavīra* flowers.
One should offer *karṇikāra* flowers;
one obtains a hundred *dīnāras*.
One who desires the position of a commander-in-chief should offer *kunda* flowers.
One obtains the rank of commander-in-chief;
by offering *tārāvartta* flowers,
one obtains a thousand *dīnāra*s.
One should offer a hundred thousand oblations of *mucilinda* flowers;
one obtains a thousand pieces of gold.
By offering white *karavīra* flowers, one becomes bound by a triple band.
One who maintains the support [of the ritual] also attains the desired object. Having kindled a fire in front of the cloth painting, worship should be performed, increasing day by day.
One should offer a thousand oblations of gold, each the size of a *tuṭi*, anointed with fragrant oil, until the Blessed One becomes a granter of boons.
Then he becomes a universal monarch of the Vidyādharas; whatever he desires,
he should offer as an oblation silver powder.
One bestows a kingdom.
One should offer iron powder as an oblation;
one obtains a thousand dīnāras.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of saffron smeared with scented oil;
one obtains whatever one prays for.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of all types of fragrant substances.
One obtains whatever object is desired.
One should offer a hundred thousand oblations of camphor;
one obtains a hundred thousand dīnāras.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of sandalwood fuel-sticks smeared with scented oil;
one obtains a thousand dīnāras. One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of gold and cloth.
One obtains a thousand dīnāras.
One should offer a hundred thousand pieces of agalloch wood as fuel;
one becomes a possessor of the Veda.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of *dhāsa* wood fuel sticks smeared with fragrant oil;
the pacification of great diseases occurs.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of nimba fruits smeared with fragrant oil; this liberates one from all bonds.
Having taken the clarified butter from a cow that has a calf of the same age, one should drink it after consecrating it one hundred thousand times;
one becomes wise.
One should offer one hundred thousand arka flowers as oblations.
One becomes beloved by all sentient beings.
Having consecrated flowers and fruit seven times with mantras, whoever they are given to shall become submissive.

On the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight, one who observes the *poṣadha* vow should smear a mandala with fallen cow dung at a shrine containing relics (*sadhātuka-caitya*). Having performed worship with perfumes, flowers, and lamps of ghee, and having kindled a fire with *udumbara* wood, one should offer eight thousand oblations of *brahmī* fuel sticks.
One who eats sacrificial food becomes wise.
For the subjugation of a Brahmin, one should offer milk into the fire;
he then becomes submissive.
One should offer the sacrificial oblation (haviṣya) belonging to a Kṣatriya;
he becomes submissive.
For the subjugation of a Vaiśya, one should offer the sacrificial oblation mixed with barley and curd, having combined them together.
One becomes submissive.
Upon seeing an enemy, one should recite [the mantra];
he becomes paralyzed.
With water consecrated seven times, one fulfills all hopes.
For all diseases, there is cleansing with it.
One should anoint the eyes with a *lōdhra* pill consecrated seven times.
It removes eye disease.
For one who is ill, a thread should be tied after it has been consecrated seven times;
then all seizing spirits have no power.
With ashes over which the mantra has been recited seven times, there is the binding of a mandala; by tying it around the topknot, self-protection is achieved.
With a clod of earth over which the mantra has been recited seven times, there is the binding of the directions.
For a woman having difficult labor, oil should be given after it has been consecrated with the recitation [of the mantra].
She will give birth easily.

For a woman with a difficult labor who has bathed after her menstrual period, one should empower cow’s milk one hundred and eight times with the mantra; having caused her to prostrate to all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, it should be given for her to drink.
She should also be fed excellent rice porridge mixed with ghee.

Then she gives birth to a son who is handsome. Beginning from the first day of the bright fortnight, one should install the cloth painting facing east and offer eight thousand pills of guggulu incense every day at the three junctions of the day.
He gives whatever one desires.

Having performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*), having installed the cloth painting (*paṭa*) at a reliquary stūpa (*sadhātuka-caitya*), and having offered perfumes, flowers, incense, and a sacrificial oblation (*bali*), one should offer as an oblation before the painting for seven nights, three times each day, *agaru* wood fuel-sticks the size of a thumb-joint, anointed with *turuṣka* oil.
He bestows a kingdom.
It bestows the state of a Vidyādhara, invisibility, the power of moving through the air on foot, or the faculty of retaining all that is heard.

Now, for one desiring to accomplish the pill (*guḷikā*): one should combine the filaments of *karṇikāra*, *nāgakesara*, white sandalwood, and elephant ichor; having made a pill and dried it in the shade, one should grind it with the hands of a girl wearing clean clothes.
This should be performed under the Puṣya constellation.

Having become pure, one should place seven pills encased in three metals inside a casket of black agarwood and recite the mantra before the cloth painting until it makes a rattling sound (*khaṭakhaṭāyati*).
Taking that [casket] and giving one to the Blessed One, and having placed it in his mouth, one becomes invisible.
Before the cloth painting, one should offer eight thousand oblations of *lakṣa* seeds smeared with curd, honey, and ghee.
One obtains a treasure.
One should offer eight thousand oblations of *kadamba* flowers smeared with curd, honey, and ghee;
all sentient beings will become submissive.
Having descended to a river that flows to the ocean, one who has observed the fast should offer eight thousand *kesara* flowers;
he will obtain ten pairs of garments.
Before the cloth painting (*paṭa*), one should offer eight thousand *jāti* flowers smeared with curds, honey, and ghee at the three junctions of the day.
For seven days,
one becomes beloved by all sentient beings;
one bestows and receives their realms.

One should offer eight thousand oblations of white water-lily flowers smeared with curd, honey, and ghee for seven days; one will obtain the five sense-objects. For the subjugation of a king, one should offer royal mustard seeds.
For seven nights,
for the purpose of subjugating a Brāhmaṇa, one should offer eight thousand oblations of Karaṇṭaka flowers for seven nights.
For the subjugation of a Vaiśya, one should offer eight thousand *saugandhika* flowers into the fire for seven nights.

For the subjugation of a Śūdra, one should offer eight thousand [offerings] into the fire for seven nights. For a widow (*raṇḍā*), one should offer eight thousand fuel-sticks of *vaikaṅkata* wood into the fire for seven nights.
Having consecrated eight thousand recitations of *rocanā* at a reliquary containing relics, one should go to the royal court;
all will become submissive.
One should offer eight thousand oblations of *dūrvā* grass sprouts.
Peace comes to another.
One who desires to bring peace upon oneself should offer milk as an oblation at the three junctions of the day;
peace will then be attained.
Having placed ghee in a copper vessel before the southern form of Mahādeva, one should recite the mantra a thousand times and offer a *bali* sacrifice consisting of all types of food;
then the ghee will move.
Then one becomes accomplished.
Having applied a tilaka mark on the forehead, one becomes beloved by all people.

To increase intelligence, having performed worship of the Blessed One Amitābha and the noble Mañjuśrī, one should place ghee in either silver or copper and recite the mantra until the threefold accomplishment is attained.
Having drunk it, one becomes wise;
when it smokes, one gains invisibility;
and when it blazes, one travels through the sky.
One who desires to accomplish *manaḥśilā* should subsist on milk and barley gruel and recite the mantra one hundred thousand times.

Having fasted for three nights before Mahādeva, having established [the substance] upon seven *aśvattha* leaves and covered it with three [more], and having offered a *bali* sacrifice consisting of all kinds of nourishing substances,
he should perform protection for himself and his companions without restriction and recite the mantra until the threefold accomplishment is attained.

By means of the blazing [mantra], one lives for ten thousand years. Having fashioned an iron wheel or a trident, having performed a grand worship, and holding it in the right hand, one should sit cross-legged before the cloth painting and recite [the mantra] until it makes a crackling sound and blazes forth.
Having taken that, one becomes a vidyādhara;
all gods and humans become subject to one's will.
One desiring to perform the rite of the finger (aṅgulisādhana) should take earth from both banks of a river and have a finger made from it.
Having placed that finger in front of the cloth painting,
one should draw it forth until it comes;
then it becomes accomplished.
She brings whoever she causes to be summoned.

One who desires to accomplish *rocanā* (yellow pigment), having performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*), should establish it before a painted image (*paṭa*), offer perfumes, flowers, and incense, and recite the mantra until it blazes with light.
By that accomplishment, one lives for five thousand years.

One who desires to accomplish the lotus should fashion a lotus out of red sandalwood, install the cloth-painting in a shrine containing relics, and taking it before that [shrine], perform the preliminary practice and recite the mantra until it blazes. Having taken it [once it blazes], one becomes a universal monarch of all vidyādharas. The gods who frequent Kailāsa become subject to one's will.

One becomes invincible to all vidyādharas. Poison is neutralized by water. One may command fevers and the like. By reciting [the mantra] once over one who is possessed, that person is made healthy; it provides self-protection.
With water over which the mantra has been recited once, protection for one's companions is achieved;
with three recitations, the binding of the directions;
and with four recitations, the binding of the mandala.

Having fasted for a full day and night on the eighth day of the dark fortnight, one should fashion an image of Noble Mañjuśrī using the unfallen cow dung of a tawny cow that has a calf of the same color. Having placed it facing the east and performed a great worship, one should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times before it.
Then the Blessed One will nod his head, or else he will manifest some other sign of accomplishment.
Then one becomes accomplished;
whatever one contemplates, all that one performs.
The Blessed One becomes the granter of boons.
It fulfills all desires and,
in dreams, declares what is auspicious and inauspicious;
one may employ it as desired.

In the forenoon, by reciting [the mantra] one thousand times, a fistful of food is produced. One who observes the *poṣadha* vows, subsisting on a diet of milk and barley-gruel, should ascend a mountain peak and recite it one hundred thousand times;
then a vision occurs.
One accomplishes one's desire. Having performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*), one should offer eight thousand oblations of *kunduruka* resin before the cloth painting for seven nights.
One becomes a king in a single region.
One should offer eight thousand grains at the three junctions of the day throughout the entire night.
One obtains one hundred dīnāras.
Having kindled a fire with *āṭaruṣaka* wood, one should offer eight thousand *āṭaruṣaka* flowers smeared with ghee;
one obtains gold.
Having fasted for a day and a night on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, one should offer eight thousand oblations of mustard seeds smeared with ghee;
one will obtain a thousand gold coins,
or else a village.
Having kindled a fire with *śleṣmātaka* wood in front of the cloth painting, one should offer a hundred thousand oblations of young *dūrvā* shoots for three nights;
one will obtain a thousand cows.
One should offer eight thousand oblations of *surasī* leaves.
One obtains a divine house.
By reciting [the mantra] one hundred thousand times mentally, one obtains a thousand *purāṇas*.
One should offer a thousand *śrīpiṣṭaka* cakes three times a day for seven nights.
One obtains a thousand dīnāras;
one accomplishes everything according to one's desire;
and one becomes possessed of glory.
He becomes fortunate;
if one performs a fire offering with red flowers by a river,
one obtains red garments.

On the eighth or the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight, in a secluded spot on the ground beneath a white *arka* tree, one should offer perfumes, flowers, incense, garlands, and so forth to the noble Mañjuśrī and recite the mantra eight thousand times. Afterwards, one should have an image of the noble Mañjuśrī made, the size of a thumb-joint.
On the eighth day of the bright fortnight, in a secluded place at an anthill, one should offer white perfumes, oblations, garlands, and incense and recite the mantra eight thousand times.
Then, having taken earth from an anthill, one should knead it with scented water.

Using that clay, one should fashion a counter-seal (pratimudrā) for the previously made seal of the image using the milk of an Arka plant. Then, beginning from the first day of the bright fortnight until the eighth day, having performed worship to the Blessed One three times a day, one should offer a sacrificial oblation (bali).
Thereafter, he should be struck with eight thousand *jātī* flowers.
One who observes the *poṣadha* vows, subsists on a diet of milk and barley, and sleeps upon a bed of *darbha* grass should accomplish this;
he obtains a thousand *dīnāras*.
By constant recitation, he attains success in his journey.
If one recites it seven or eight thousand times for seven days,
one obtains a village and becomes possessed of glory.
One who desires to produce wealth should go to a cow-pen on the eighth day of the dark fortnight and, subsisting on milk and barley-gruel, recite the mantra one hundred thousand times.
On the fourteenth day of the subsequent dark fortnight, having fasted for a day and night, he should recite it another hundred thousand times in that very place.
He will obtain eight hundred dīnāras.
Whatever one desires—be it gold or a village—one obtains it.

Having fasted for a day and night on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, one should kindle a fire before the cloth painting with wood from the Bodhi tree and recite the mantra eight thousand times over *vacā* root; one will obtain a hundred *dīnāras*.

On the eighth day of the dark fortnight, having kindled a fire with *palāśa* wood, one should offer one hundred thousand pellets of *guggulu* resin smeared with curd, honey, and clarified butter before the cloth painting;
one will obtain one hundred *dīnāras*.
One should offer one hundred thousand *śatapuṣpa* flowers.
One obtains one hundred dīnāras.
One should offer one hundred thousand fuel-sticks of *bilva*;
whatever one desires, that he accomplishes.

On the bank of the Ganges river, or on a seashore, in a place that is uninhabited by humans and undisturbed, one should construct a stūpa out of sand measuring one span of the Sugata. Having offered perfumes, flowers, and incense according to one's means, one should perform the consecration eight thousand times with mantras.

Thus, offering perfumes and so forth day after day until one thousand and eight stūpas are completed, one attains the binding of the turban; one should also offer eight thousand oblations of sesame seeds.
Whomever one desires, that person comes under one's control.
Having performed worship at a relic-containing caitya, one should recite the mantra eight thousand times;
it will then declare what is auspicious and what is inauspicious.
Desiring to perform the rite of nourishment (*āpyāyana*), one should offer eight thousand oblations of fuel-sticks from a milk-tree smeared with clarified butter before the Blessed One.
Thereby, that vidyā becomes nourished.
This should be employed during the seventh stage of practice (*sādhana*).
Having gone to a place where a *brahmarākṣasa* or another being who has performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*) resides, one should recite [the mantra] ten thousand times;
it will bestow a great treasure.
Subsisting on milk and barley-gruel, one should recite it for one year at a reliquary (*caitya*) containing sacred relics (*sadhātuka*).

Having installed the cloth painting (*paṭa*) in that very place, having fasted for three nights on the eighth day of the dark fortnight, having performed a grand worship and offered a sacrificial oblation (*bali*), one should kindle a fire before the painting and offer eight thousand oblations of *vaṭa* tree wood fuel sticks smeared with curd, honey, and ghee.
The yakṣas, headed by Kubera, will arrive;

one must not be afraid. Having established [the painting] there and sat upon a well-formed cushion in the cross-legged posture (*paryaṅka*), holding it with the hand, one should recite the mantra until it blazes forth.
In the meantime, it pacifies the suffering of all those in the hells and the animal realm.
Assemblies of vidyādharas gather there;
then, having paid homage to all the buddhas and bodhisattvas, it should be taken up.
Followed by the Vidyādharas, he goes to the City of Vidyādharas;
he becomes a king of the Vidyādharas,
and all the Vidyādharas worship him.
One becomes a dweller for a great eon (*mahākalpa*).
By this procedure, specific weapons such as the discus, sword, and mallet are to be accomplished.

If that vidyā, while being practiced, is not successful, one should perform worship before the Blessed Buddha and the painted image (*paṭa*), and recite the mantra eight thousand times in conjunction with it.
There, one should sleep upon a bed of *kuśa* grass.
In whatever place one seeks what is deficient or in excess, there the preliminary service (*pūrvasevā*) is performed together with a *yakṣa* and a *yakṣiṇī*.
Having smeared a mandala there, one should offer eight thousand oblations of white mustard seeds.
She comes;
she may be addressed as desired;
when requested, she gives it.
By eating that, one becomes possessed of a lifespan lasting for an eon (kalpa).
If she does not come, one should perform the rite for seven nights;
then she comes.
Then, one desiring to perform a rite of pacification (*śānti*) should offer eight thousand oblations of milk before the Blessed One, or sprinkle [the area] with scented water;
thus peace is attained.
Or, one should wipe away the venom from one bitten by a snake using a sprout or a peacock's eye-feather.
One becomes free from poison.
Having ascended the summit of an anthill, fasting and standing on one foot, one should recite [the mantra] from the forenoon until the afternoon;
whatever karma is to be experienced will be exhausted.
In that place where he resides,
there is the preliminary service (*pūrvasevā*).
Having gone there and having smeared a mandala, one should offer eight thousand oblations of white mustard seeds (*gaurasarṣapa*).
The yakṣas arrive.
An offering (arghya) should be presented with a flask of scented water previously prepared.
The yakṣas ask, "What should be done?"
"We have been summoned.
"It should be said: 'May the yakṣas indeed be obedient to our commands.
Having said, "So be it," the yakṣas disappear.
They become accomplished;
they grant whatever one seeks,
and they bestow divine elixirs, rejuvenators, and medicinal preparations.
Then, even for one surrounded by a thousand followers, he provides food of six flavors;
whatever he seeks, all that he provides.

Thus, for the purpose of subjugation, having fasted for three nights with either of the two black [substances], having performed the protection rites and being well-restrained, one should offer eight thousand pills of guggulu incense into smokeless coals before the cloth painting.
When [the offerings] are anointed with ghee,
the deity arrives at midnight;
she should be addressed.
They bestow medicinal herbs, or whatever one may seek. One who desires clothing should offer eight thousand oblations of *dūrvā* stalks smeared with ghee; he shall obtain garments.
Having consecrated *vacā* root eight thousand times with mantras and placing it in one's mouth, one becomes the superior disputant in all legal proceedings.
Having recited [the mantra] over fragrant oil and anointed the face,
one becomes the superior disputant in royal courts.
Having consecrated collyrium eight thousand times with mantras, one should apply it to the eyes;
in legal proceedings, one becomes the winning party.
Or, during an eclipse of the moon or sun, having placed *śrotāñjana* in the mouth, one should recite the mantra as long as the eclipse lasts until it is released.
Having nourished [the deity] and performed protection, and having consecrated the ointment eight thousand times with mantras, one should apply it to the eyes;
one becomes invisible.
One should offer a hundred thousand oblations of all kinds of perfumes before the cloth painting.
He beholds prosperity;
whatever boon he seeks,
that he obtains.
Remaining silent and subsisting on alms, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times;
one becomes invisible.
Having smeared a mandala in front of the cloth painting and scattered flowers upon it, one should drink seven handfuls of water consecrated with the mantra for seven days.
One becomes intelligent,
and what was previously studied does not perish.
Having recited [the mantra] one hundred and eight times over a karṣa of *brahmī* juice and a karṣa of milk, it should be drunk.
Day after day the clouds increase;
for twenty-one nights they hold and sustain five hundred [clouds].
Protection is to be afforded by placing water over which the mantra has been recited seven times upon the head.
This constitutes the binding of the mandala.
One effects possession by means of twenty-one stakes of khadira wood over which the mantra has been recited twenty-one times, using guggulu incense.
Treatment with a poison-smeared knife, or the destruction of planetary influences with a sprout;
bathe those seized by planets with white flowers or guggulu incense over which the mantra has been recited seven times;
a thread should be tied [around the wrist].
One should offer oblations of white mustard seeds mixed with sesame and smeared with ghee;
one becomes eloquent.
The oblation should be performed at night.

At a reliquary containing relics, on the full moon day, having respectfully smeared a maṇḍala, one should recite the mantra while offering eight full jars, eight flower garlands, and incense of agallochum, turuṣka, sandalwood, and kunduru.
Then, it bestows the accomplishment of the body.
At a reliquary containing relics, subsisting on milk and barley gruel, one should perform worship according to one's means and recite the mantra one hundred thousand times.
One becomes capable of performing rites such as paralyzing (*jambhana*) and deluding (*mohana*).
Having consumed barley meal (*saktubhakṣaḥ*), one should descend into a river up to the depth of the armpits and recite the mantra one hundred thousand times (*lakṣa*).
One then becomes highly proficient in the applications of subjugation (*vaśīkaraṇa*), invisibility (*antardhāna*), and the use of stones and other materials.
One should offer cotton seeds at the abode of the nāgas;
the nāgas will become submissive,
and whatever one seeks, that one obtains.
Having consecrated the fingers of the right hand eight times with the mantra, one should threaten an elephant; it will become submissive.
By this very same procedure, one paralyzes elephants, tigers, buffaloes, and so forth.

Through an oblation of sesame seeds, there is the subjugation of men and women. Through the sale of [the empowered] grain, there is protection—protection for oneself and protection for others. With sevenfold consecration, there is the binding of the topknot (*śikhābandha*).
In battle, in royal courts, or in disputes, victory comes to one who performs the recitation (*japa*).

If one desires to perform an empowerment (*abhiṣeka*) upon oneself, one should take four jars filled with water from a river, a pond, or a spring that is not in its proper season, or otherwise, having cast all types of fragrant seeds into them and consecrated them eight thousand times with mantras, one should sprinkle oneself with that water.
One becomes completely freed from all obstacles, Vināyakas, and misfortune.
In the case of a Piśāca fever, one should sprinkle [the patient] with scented water over which the mantra has been recited eight hundred times;
he will become healthy.

Having prepared a *vetāḍa* by driving well-consecrated stakes of *khadira* wood toward the east and *vālāśallaka* wood [into its body], and having stationed men with swords in their hands with great care in the four directions, one should sit upon the heart of the *vetāḍa* and offer iron filings with an iron ladle (*sruva*).
From its mouth, a tongue emerges;
having severed it with a sharp weapon, it becomes a sword resembling a blue lotus.
When it is grasped by him, he flies up together with his retinue;
he becomes a king of the Vidyādharas and lives for eleven hundred million years.
When his time has come, he is reborn among the gods.

Having fashioned a *muṇḍi* made of *puṣpaloha* endowed with the [proper] characteristics, and having performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*) before the cloth painting, having consecrated it for seven nights, and having offered a thousand oblations (*sahasrasampātāhuti*) before the Blessed One on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight while fasting for three nights; having performed a magnificent worship, having arranged the offerings, and having established the protection, the mandala-binding, and the boundary-binding; and having fed the noble Saṅgha according to one's ability, prostrating at their feet and having obtained the permission of the noble Saṅgha, one dies.
Having placed a heap of white mustard seeds before the cloth painting, one should offer them after reciting the mantra over the heap.
This effects the expulsion of all planetary seizures (*graha*). By means of guggulu incense, it pacifies all untimely deaths and arrests all winds and clouds.
Having recited the mantra over mustard seeds while performing the *jāpa*, one should cast them into the sky with firm resolve;
this effects the immobilization of all clouds.
A stake of *khadira* wood, consecrated seven times with the mantra, should be driven in.
One becomes free from poison.
In all cases of strife, quarrel, conflict, and dispute, one should empower a five-colored thread eight hundred times with mantras and wear it in a secret place;
all strife, quarrels, conflicts, and disputes will then be paralyzed.
For all purposes regarding mantras, water should be given after reciting [the mantra] seven times;
one becomes free from poison.
One who desires wealth, being pure and dressed in clean garments, having fasted for a day and night, should offer *kunduruka* incense before the cloth painting (*paṭa*).
In a dream, he reveals what is auspicious or inauspicious.
One obtains seven thousand *rūpakas*.

For the sake of enjoyment, one who desires wealth should establish the cloth-painting at the confluence of rivers, in a pond, or in some other pure location; having done so, one should begin the recitation (*jāpa*) and fire-oblation (*homa*) using the ashes of all the *mudrās* that have been broken.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of lotuses smeared with curd, honey, and ghee,
or two hundred thousand;
thereupon, one attains all desires.
By performing three hundred thousand homas, one bestows a kingdom;
by performing twenty-one thousand homas, one becomes a great lord of wealth.
One should offer eight thousand oblations of guggulu pills smeared with curd, honey, and clarified butter.
For twenty-one nights,
prosperity arises;
one obtains a thousand dīnāras.
It should be thrown against a wall;
all enemies will become paralyzed.
Having prepared a mandala of cow dung, taken a thread, placed it in the center of the mandala, and offered guggulu incense, one should recite the mantra.
If he is alive, the thread moves;
if he is not alive, it does not move.
Having smeared a mandala with cow dung, measuring four cubits in size, and having offered flowers and incense, one should recite the mantra while standing right there to paralyze enemies.
Having recited the mantra over a weapon seven times, it should be buried in the ground;
all enemies will be cut down. Having recited the mantra seven times over the army of an enemy kingdom, it should be cast away.
One becomes invulnerable;
it is a destroyer of epilepsy.
Having kindled a fire with *apāmārga* fuel-sticks, one should offer oblations of black sesame seeds mixed with white *karavīra* flowers.
The seizure-demons of epilepsy are destroyed.
In all fevers, a black thread should be tied [around the wrist]. In all cases of seizing spirits and ḍākinīs, a blue thread should be tied.
The cutting of a piece of iron smeared with the earth from a mountain slope where a tumor has appeared becomes white clay.
Having observed a fast during an eclipse of the moon or sun for the sake of all sentient beings, one should recite the mantra over oil.
One should then smear the face with that oil.
One should enter the enemy's camp;
a mind of loving-kindness will arise.
By this very procedure, having empowered the *pratisarā* mantra eight thousand times and binding it upon the hand, one may enter into battle.
One becomes invincible.
Having risen at dawn and prepared a cow-dung mandala at a shrine containing relics, one should take two handfuls of water, recite the mantra over each seven times, and then measure it out;
one should drink it without speaking.
Then, at the time of the morning tide, one should eat after reciting the first mantra three times;
at the evening tide, one should sleep after reciting it one hundred and eight times.
In this way, all activities are purified.
Purity of speech arises;
one learns a hundred verses day by day.
Thus, for seven days, having consecrated water seven times with the recitation [of the mantra], the power of the finger is accomplished.
Then, one draws [the mantra] onto a finger;
whoever is touched by it becomes submissive. Having recited the mantra over clay, it should be applied as a binding.
If one is bound, it becomes severed. For abdominal pain, one should recite [the mantra] seven times over the hand and wipe [the area];
one will become healthy.

Having recited [the mantra] over the corner of the robe three times, one should tie the corner of the robe; thus the thieves will be bound. Having recited [the mantra] over oil, it should be applied to the body.
Whatever one gives, that one receives.

Having made a mandala of cow dung, having filled an iron vessel with flowers and ashes, and having placed it in the center of the mandala, one should recite the *tūlikā* mantra one hundred and eight times and stand upon it.
Having offered *guggulu* incense, one should snap the fingers while reciting the mantra.
Wherever a thief goes, one should draw a mandala with ashes; he becomes submissive.

For the immobilization of all beings through mental concentration, one should kindle a fire before a cloth painting on the full moon of the bright fortnight using wood from a Bodhi tree and offer eight thousand sesame seeds as oblations;
he becomes submissive.
Having consecrated a stake of *khadira* wood by reciting [the mantra] one hundred and eight times, one should bury it in the four directions;
thus the boundary is established and the mandala is secured.
By sprinkling water over sentient beings twenty-one times with the mantra recited, they are driven away.
If one recites it before an angry person while holding mustard seeds, that person becomes appeased.
Now, if one desires to bring a king under control, one should offer ten thousand oblations of fuel-sticks from *arka* wood, smeared with curd, honey, and ghee, before the cloth painting (*paṭa*).
One becomes submissive.
This is the ritual for subduing with a finger:
having offered incense, flowers, and perfumes before the cloth painting, one should place the right index finger upon seven *aśvattha* leaves and recite the mantra ten thousand times.
One should give dināras and garments to a third person;
one should offer eight thousand oblations of ghee;
one becomes possessed of intelligence.
One should offer eight thousand *nāgakeśara* flowers;
a maiden will appear.
One should offer eight thousand *jātī* flowers.
One obtains garments;
by reciting the mantra one hundred thousand times, one becomes a rememberer of past lives;
there are seven hundred types of diseases.
Having performed the preliminary rite (*puraścaraṇa*) by subsisting on milk and barley-gruel for one hundred thousand repetitions,
one should fast for three nights on the eighth day of the bright fortnight, perform a grand worship of the cloth painting (*paṭa*), and recite the mantra until a ray of light issues forth;
then one becomes accomplished (*siddha*).
Whatever one contemplates in the mind— whether it be sovereignty or the state of a Vidyadhara— one obtains that very thing.
Merely by reciting it, all evil friends are paralyzed,
and all obstacles and Vinayakas are destroyed.

Having wrapped it with red thread and placed it within a pair of earthenware bowls, one should perform worship before a reliquary containing relics or before an image, and recite the mantra until the threefold accomplishment occurs.
When [the object] becomes warm, one can travel five hundred *yojanas* by foot;
furthermore, all those who travel on foot become subject to one's control.
When it begins to smoke, he becomes invisible;
if he does not touch the ground with his feet by a distance of four finger-breadths,
he lives for a thousand years.
One travels a thousand yojanas;
one possesses the strength of ten men;
and when [the fire] blazes, one lives for three kalpas.

One becomes a Vidyādhara and becomes invincible. On a full-moon day of the month of Pauṣa, having observed the poṣadha vows, one should offer ten thousand lotuses smeared with curd, honey, and ghee before the cloth painting.
Then, a divine woman rises from the fire-pit and offers a boon:
"She should be taken as either a mother or a sister."
From that time forward, subsisting on a diet of milk and barley-gruel, one should recite [the mantra] two hundred thousand times.

At the conclusion, having fasted for three nights, one should perform worship before a reliquary (*caitya*) containing relics or before an image on the fifteenth day. Then, in the presence of the Blessed One, one should recite upon a bed of *aśvattha* leaves until a woman of divine form appears.
Having offered her the guest-offering (*argha*), one should request a boon.
She bestows devotion, ornaments, and clothing;
one lives for a thousand years.

During a lunar eclipse, having taken fresh butter from a cow that has a calf of the same color, and having fashioned a doll measuring six finger-breadths, one who has fasted for four meals should prepare a bed of *aśvattha* leaves, recite the mantra eight thousand times, and then consume it.
All kings will come under one's control.

Taking a piece of *kanakavīcikā* and *manaḥśilā*, on the full moon day of the fifteenth, having performed a magnificent worship while observing the *poṣadha* vows, one should strike the heart [of the king] with eight thousand fragrant flowers.
For the remainder of the time, one should recite the mantra continuously.
One obtains five hundred dīnāras.
Having performed worship on the Poṣadha day, one should recite [the mantra] one thousand times;
it reveals auspicious and inauspicious matters in dreams.
One should offer oblations of [substances] smeared with ghee three times a day for seven days;
one should recite the mantra eight thousand times. This brings even a king under one's control.
Having kindled a fire with wood from the *rājavṛkṣa* tree, one should pierce a doll made of *madana* wood adorned with all ornaments with a needle and heat it so that it does not melt.
By reciting the mantra eight hundred times at the three junctions of the day, one can summon [the target] even from the underworld (*pātāla*).
Having fashioned a six-finger-long wooden statue of a girl out of *aśoka* wood, one should take it, ascend a mountain peak, and recite the mantra one hundred thousand times.
Subsisting on milk and barley gruel, by reciting it one hundred thousand times, one obtains a village;
by reciting it two hundred thousand times, one performs whatever actions one desires.
By reciting it three hundred thousand times, one exhausts the obscurations of karma;
by reciting it four hundred thousand times, Noble Mañjuśrī grants a vision;
and by reciting it five hundred thousand times, the purification of a buddha-field occurs.
By reciting six hundred thousand times, one is reborn in whichever world-system one desires.
By reciting seven hundred thousand times, one obtains a dhāraṇī.
One who wishes to arrest fire should recite [the mantra] over a strip of cloth seven times and place it in the mouth.
In water, this very same accomplishment is achieved.
In a dispute, having consecrated a thread one hundred and eight times with mantras, three knots should be made;
thus one becomes the proponent of the superior argument.

Having placed a *pala* of cow’s ghee in a vessel on the fifteenth day, and having offered a *gomaya*-maṇḍala and agarwood incense before the noble Mañjuśrī, one should recite the mantra one hundred and eight times and then drink it.
Having drunk it, one must not sleep;
thus one becomes wise.

For seven days, there shall be the dispatching of fever, the dispatching of spirits, self-protection, the raising of a *vetāḍa*, entry into a cave, entry into a forest, protection, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the directions; by means of recitation (*jāpa*), thieves, tigers, and *ḍākinīs* are paralyzed.
One who desires to become invisible should take the root of *śatāvarī*, empower it one thousand times with mantras, and bind it [to oneself];
he becomes invisible.
One should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times before the cloth painting.

Then, having purchased *śatapuṣpā* flowers from a hero-seller, one should offer them as oblations smeared with curd, honey, and ghee. Whatever price they were purchased for, the result becomes a hundredfold that amount.
The fire offering (homa) should be performed for seven days;
one should offer eight thousand *sumana* fuel-sticks for seven days,
and one will obtain wealth.
One should recite [the mantra] for one month before a cloth painting;
one will obtain four *dīnāra*s.
Having consecrated a *marīca* fruit seven times with the mantra and placed it in one's mouth, one may converse with whomever one chooses.
He is regarded as having a son.
Having performed [the rite] before a Buddha image in a shrine containing relics, one should cast [it] into water;
for fishermen, there will be no fish.
One should offer eight thousand oblations of *śephālikā* flowers.
One should offer incense made from horse dung over which the mantra has been recited seven times; thus, bedbugs will not appear.
By reciting [the mantra] one hundred thousand times over a flower or a fruit, mosquitoes will not appear;
this is a means of subjugation (*vaśīkaraṇa*).

[This rite brings about] access to the king’s gate, the chewing of tooth-sticks, the giving of fruit, the giving of perfumes, the binding of the earth, the binding of thieves, the paralyzing of all fangs, the causing of paralysis, the breaking of fetters, the stopping of water, the stopping of fire, the cleansing of poison, the transference of poison, the binding of poison, the subjugation of spirits (*bhūta*), and liberation from *ḍākinīs* and seizing demons. Having written [the mantra] on birch bark with ox-gall for a lost spell, one should recite it one hundred times before the Blessed One at a shrine containing relics.
At dawn, it becomes perfected.
Having recited [the mantra] seven times over white mustard seeds, one should scatter them in a village or a city.
Those who dwell there will sleep as if dead until sunrise.

One who desires to bring under one's control a woman or a man should recite the mantra eight thousand times at an improper time (vikāla), facing the direction in which that person’s house lies, and then go to sleep.
They will grant an audience.
By doing this for seven days, they become submissive.

By sprinkling water over which the mantra has been recited seven times, the mouths of all fanged creatures are bound. One should perform the binding of medicinal herbs and the binding of the treasure-store mentally; one should bury stakes of *khadira* wood at twenty-one locations for the treasure-store, specifically in the four corners.
By this very procedure, one remains for an eon and is honored by all the accomplished masters (*siddhas*), [attaining mastery over] the alms-bowl, sword, water-pot, and so forth.

During a lunar eclipse, a monk should cause [the mantra] to be heard by all these [beings]. One who dwells in the ritual code (*kalpasthāyin*) and practices celibacy (*brahmacārin*) moves with unimpeded gait and wanders at will. Subsisting on cow-urine and barley-gruel, one should recite [the mantra] two hundred thousand times; one obtains eight villages.
Wherever one desires, there one remains.
Having installed the cloth painting on the seashore, one should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times;
the Sāgara Nāga King will then lead one into his own abode,
where one finds the wish-fulfilling gem (cintāmaṇi).
When it is held, one becomes a performer of all rites;
one also goes to the buddha-field of the Tathāgata, remaining for an eon, unimpeded.
One should make knots with a thread spun by a virgin and consecrated eight thousand times;
