all obstacles and Vināyakas will be destroyed.
Subsisting on alms, one should recite the mantra three hundred thousand times on a riverbank.
Eating only sacrificial food (haviṣya), one should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times at the confluence of rivers;
one becomes invisible and becomes the master of all those who possess the power of invisibility.

Having taken a bowl that conforms to the measurements prescribed in the Vinaya, one should sit cross-legged before the cloth painting and, holding the bowl with the right hand, recite the mantra until it blazes.
One then becomes a Vidyādhara.
Wherever such a person dwells, there prosperity shall prevail.
Thus, there are immeasurable qualities.
Now, if one wishes to bring about peace, one should recite [the mantra] eight thousand times over fragrant flowers smeared with curd, honey, and ghee;
supreme peace will ensue.
For nourishment (*pauṣṭika*):

having kindled a fire with fuel-sticks from milk-trees, one should offer eight thousand oblations of sesame, rice, mung beans, black gram, and so forth, along with women who have been anointed with curd, honey, and ghee.
Supreme nourishment occurs,
whether with a cloth or without a cloth;
one who observes the poṣadha vows, is embraced by the three refuges, and possesses the bodhicitta, should recite [the mantra] ten thousand times.

Then, on the full moon day or during a lunar eclipse, having offered a bali-oblation for the fulfillment of all desires and having fasted for a day and night, one should recite the mantra throughout the entire night.
Thereafter, one becomes capable of performing all rites and remains unimpeded in all directions.
By merely forming the mental image, one brings [the patient] back to life.
One should send water over which the mantra has been recited seven times;
having drunk it, the afflicted person becomes healthy.
The flight of the planetary spirits (*graha*) is accomplished by a thousandfold oblation of mustard seeds.
Having installed the cloth painting at the entrance of an asura cave, one who observes the ritual precepts (*niyama*) should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times.
An asura maiden will emerge and lead one inside.
Having placed it in the mouth of the speech, one should recite [the mantra] until the threefold accomplishment is attained:
when it becomes warm, there is subjugation;
when it emits smoke, invisibility; and when it blazes, the power of traveling through the sky.
Having installed a cloth painting in a reliquary containing relics, one should begin on the eighth day of the bright fortnight and offer one hundred thousand lotuses into the fire;
one will become a king.
One should have a staff made of red sandalwood, sixteen or twelve finger-breadths in length, by a craftsman who observes the *poṣadha* vows.
Then, one should recite [the mantra] three hundred thousand times before the painting.
Having fasted for a day and night and performed a grand worship on the full moon day, one should take a wooden staff in the right hand and recite it until the threefold accomplishment is attained.
When it begins to emit heat, one becomes the superior debater among all opponents.
If it smokes, there is invisibility;
if it blazes, one travels through the sky. Having wrapped oneself entirely in a white cloth, one should recite the mantra until it blazes.
He flies up with a retinue of a thousand.
One should recite the mantra before the cloth painting until the threefold accomplishment is attained.
Before the cloth painting, one should offer eight thousand oblations of apāmārga wood fuel smeared with curds, honey, and ghee.
A king or one of royal rank becomes submissive.

Subsisting on milk or vegetables and observing the *poṣadha* vows, one should recite [the mantra] three hundred thousand times at a shrine containing relics. Then, on the eighth day of the dark fortnight or the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, one should offer eight thousand oblations of black sesame seeds.
One obtains a thousand kārṣāpaṇas.
One should offer eight thousand pills of guggulu incense before the cloth painting;
whichever man or woman one desires, that person is brought under one's control.
One should offer eight thousand oblations of guggulu resin pills;
whoever one desires will become beloved by all people.
In the royal court, one becomes the superior debater;
by anointing oneself with [the powder] consecrated eight thousand times,
one becomes fortunate.

In front of the cloth painting (*paṭa*), beginning from the first day of the bright fortnight, one who subsists on milk and barley gruel (*yāvaka*), bathes three times a day, changes his garments three times, burns agallochum (*agaru*), turuṣka, and sandalwood, and offers the "three white" oblations (*triśukla*);
having offered an outer *bali* to all spirits (*sarvabhūtika*) and fragrant flowers—whether aquatic or terrestrial—as well as fragrant offerings or three lamps of cow-ghee;
finally, having fasted for three nights, a recitation (*japa*) must be performed throughout the entire night.
Whatever one prays for, that one obtains.
One should provide a meal for the Saṅgha according to one's ability.
Having installed a painting in a shrine containing relics, one should fast for three nights and offer thirty-two thousand oblations of *ariṣṭa* wood fuel smeared with curd, honey, and ghee.
Then, flames issue forth from the cloth, the earth trembles, and the flame of a lamp blazes out;
a garland of flowers quivers.
By these signs, one becomes accomplished.

Having placed *śrotāñjana* within the leaves of an *aśvattha* tree and having offered it into the fire one thousand times with the *sampāta* oblation, one is freed from great diseases by reciting [the mantra] once for six months;
one should recite it for one month, whereby one becomes one who has fulfilled his vow.
With guggulu incense, one causes the afflicted person to be possessed [by the deity].
For fevers occurring every day, every two days, every three days, every four days, and so forth,
or for the purpose of subjugating a woman, one should offer twenty-one oblations of lalāṭā smeared with honey before the cloth painting (paṭa) at the three junctions of the day for seven nights.
They become submissive;
likewise for a widow or a man.
In front of the cloth painting, one should offer eight thousand oblations of *rājārka* wood fuel sticks smeared with curd, honey, and ghee.
She becomes submissive.
For kings, queens, and others, one should offer oblations of salt at the three junctions of the day for twenty-one nights;
they will become submissive.
Having empowered one's head seven times with three [recitations] at the king's gate, one should enter;
one will become a favorite of the king.
Having empowered a peacock's eye (mayūracandraka) one hundred times, [one should apply it].
One should wipe away poison;
it is destroyed.
Having placed realgar between the leaves of an Aśvattha tree, one should recite the mantra three hundred thousand times.
It removes *gṛdhrasī* (sciatica).
For one suffering from fever, one should perform a cleansing with *kuśa* grass and tie on a thread spun by a maiden;
he will become fortunate.
One should offer one hundred thousand *karṇikāra* flowers;
one obtains twelve *koṭīs* of garments.

Having fashioned a wheel made of flower-metal (*puṣpaloha*), having installed a cloth painting (*paṭa*) at a shrine containing relics (*sadhātuka-caitya*), and having fasted for a day and night and performed a grand worship, one should take up the wheel and recite the mantra until signs appear.
Sparks of light issue forth from the wheel until it blazes;
then, one becomes accomplished.
All the hosts of Vidyādharas assemble;
together with his retinue,
he flies up as a king of the Vidyādharas, remaining for an eon, with unimpeded movement.
Rising at dawn, one should recite [the mantra] for one year;
he becomes a granter of boons.
One should recite it twenty-one hundred thousand times before the painted image.
A vidyādhara should recite [the mantra] one million one hundred thousand times;
he will see Noble Mañjuśrī. He should recite it seven hundred thousand times before the painted image.
He becomes invisible.
If one who is ill recites [the mantra] twenty-one hundred thousand times before the cloth painting,
the illness will perish.
Having performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*), one should recite [the mantra] twelve hundred thousand times. One will obtain an elixir of mercury (*rasarasāyana*);
by consuming it, one becomes free from wrinkles and grey hair.
Having recited [the mantra] two hundred thousand times, one should offer eight thousand oblations of royal mustard seeds;
the queen will become submissive,
and within seven nights she will provide wealth for him.
Excluding anything associated with sensual desire,
one should offer one hundred thousand oblations of *arka* wood fuel before the cloth painting;
one will obtain one hundred *pala* of gold.
One should offer eight thousand parched grains for seven nights; no obstacles will arise. One should offer eight thousand portions of oil-cake.
He becomes beloved by all people.
Out of three options, he obtains whichever he desires:
the state of a vidyādhara, or sovereignty, or he becomes just like the Blessed One himself.
This accomplishment is achieved by one who is compassionate, giving gifts to all sentient beings with a mind free from worldly desire.
Having fasted for a day and night and performed a grand worship of the cloth painting (*paṭa*), one should offer eight thousand oblations of *arka* wood fuel.
Whatever one desires, that very thing arrives in an instant.

Having powdered equal parts of agaru, priyaṅgu, and nāgakesara, and having placed them in a pair of earthenware bowls, one should consecrate them eight thousand times before the right image of Maheśvara. With one’s body anointed with that, one should offer eight thousand oblations in battle or to a messenger;
one becomes invincible and does not suffer untimely death.
By offering eight thousand *nāgapuṣpa* flowers before the cloth painting, a king becomes submissive.
For all diseases, one should take earth from a malignant ulcer, empower it seven times with the mantra, and apply it;
the affliction will be pacified.

Having performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*) and purified the body with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*), one who bathes three times a day and subsists on milk should perform eight hundred recitations before the original cloth painting (*mūlapaṭa*).

Afterwards, on the eighth day of the dark fortnight, having made an offering according to one's ability, one should sit upon a bundle of *kuśa* grass before the painting and offer eight thousand oblations of *vilva* wood fuel smeared with curd, honey, and ghee.
Then, a ray of light will issue from the head of Noble Mañjuśrī.
Having circumambulated the practitioner, she disappears into the image of the Blessed One;
thereafter, he beholds Noble Mañjuśrī,
if he is to become a universal monarch (cakravartin).
Then the practitioner’s hut blazes forth;
by the movement of a garland of flowers, one becomes a regional king (*māṇḍalika-rāja*).

Having made a mandala with white sandalwood before the cloth painting (*paṭa*), and having offered perfumes, incense, flowers, sacrificial food (*bali*), and ointments, one should take three hundred *kesara* flowers and consecrate them one hundred and eight times with mantras.

Having lit three ghee lamps and kindled the fire with *udumbara* wood fuel-sticks, one should consecrate each flower one hundred and eight times with mantras and offer them into the fire while they are anointed with ghee.
Whoever one desires will come under one's control within seven nights.
For one who recites this at the three times of day, even the five sins of immediate retribution (*pañcānantarya*) become attenuated.
By reciting it one hundred and eight times every day, even the sin of killing a Brahmin becomes as thin as a string.
By constant recitation, one obtains whatever village one desires.
Whomever one looks upon with the eyes, that person comes under one's control.
In debate, one should recite [the mantra], and one becomes the superior disputant;
one should offer oblations of sesame and beans to produce wealth;
one should offer eight thousand oblations of *vaṭa* shoots.
Having paid homage to all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, one should recite it ten times;
one will then obtain the faculty of hearing.
Noble Mañjuśrī should be depicted on a cloth or a fruit-skin using non-adhesive pigments, according to the previously mentioned ritual procedure.
Having performed worship before it, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times.

Sleeping on a bed of *kuśa* grass, subsisting on milk and barley gruel, bathing three times a day, and dressed in clean garments, one should perform the recitation while observing the eightfold fast (*poṣadha*), beginning from the first lunar day until the fifteenth.
Then:
It pacifies disease.

One who has performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*), subsisting on milk and cow urine or on barley gruel (*yāvaka*), bathing three times a day and observing the *poṣadha* vows, should install the cloth painting (*paṭa*) in a shrine containing relics (*sadhātuka-caitya*). Every day, a lamp of ghee should be lit, and worship should be performed with a thousand lotuses.
The recitation should be performed during the dark fortnight. On the first day of the bright fortnight, the practice should be commenced.
Having fasted for three nights and performed a grand worship on the full moon day, the all-night recitation should be performed.
As soon as it blazes, one flies up into the sky and becomes a Vidyādhara,
surrounded by a retinue of a thousand Vidyādharas. Having the appearance of a sixteen-year-old, with hair curled like earrings, he is invincible to all Vidyādharas.

The entrance [into the deity] is accomplished by means of incense; the destruction of calamities by means of a sprout; and self-protection by means of recitation (*jāpa*). Beginning on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight and continuing until the fifteenth, one who is pure, dressed in clean garments, and observing the eightfold fast (*aṣṭāṅga-poṣadha*), shall obtain whatever he seeks before the painted cloth (*paṭa*).
Having consecrated clarified butter (*ghṛta*) one hundred and eight times, he should drink it for seven days.
One becomes intelligent.
If one offers eight thousand *mallikā* flowers before the cloth painting for seven nights,
wealth will arise.

On the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight, having fasted for three nights, one should kindle a fire with *udumbara* wood and offer eight thousand oblations of *udumbara* fuel-sticks smeared with curds, honey, and ghee.
One will obtain five hundred *dīnāras*.
On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, one who observes the *poṣadha* vow should light eight thousand lamps and offer eight hundred lamp-wicks as oblations.
Thereafter, the recitation should be performed;
then one regains one's sight.
A deaf person, having entered the fragrant chamber (gandhakuṭī), should offer eight thousand lotuses consecrated with eight thousand recitations.
Peace is attained.
One should offer eight thousand oblations of *mālatī* flowers smeared with curd, honey, and ghee before the cloth painting;
peace is attained.

Having performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*), on the fifth day of the dark fortnight, one should install the cloth painting (*paṭa*) in a reliquary stupa (*sadhātuka-caitya*). Having performed a great worship and offered a magnificent sacrificial offering (*bali*), and having offered an external *bali* for all spirits (*sarvabhautika*), one should fashion a small figure (*puttalikā*) from *priyaṅgu* powder and draw it.
Having performed the binding of the mandala and the binding of the directions, seated upon a bundle of *kuśa* grass, one should recite the mantra until a meteor falls;
then one should recite again until the cloth painting trembles.
Other signs of accomplishment also arise;
then, having paid homage to all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, one flies up and becomes a Vidyādhara.
Capable of assuming any form at will, he hears from a distance of a thousand *yojanas* and is invulnerable to all *vidyādharas*.

Having performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*), having fasted for a day and night on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, and having performed a grand worship, one should take all unbroken grains (*akṣata*), adorn them with perfumes, flowers, and incense, and holding them in the right hand, recite the mantra until they burst into flames.
Having placed *rocanā* before the image of the noble Mañjuśrī on the cloth, one should recite the mantra until it blazes;
then it should be taken up.
By the mere act of taking it up, one becomes possessed of the strength of a *nāga*.
The weapons of others have no power over him;
whoever he directs with this mantra comes under his control,
and he lives for three hundred years.

Having fasted for a day and night on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, one should kindle a fire in front of the cloth painting with wood from the *bilva* tree and offer eight thousand oblations of *vaikaṅkata* fuel-sticks smeared with pungent oil.
For seven days, whichever girl one desires will become submissive.

On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, having fasted for one night, one should go to a cemetery, smear a mandala with cow-dung that has not fallen to the ground, take an unbroken skull-cup, wash it with red sandalwood paste, and worship it with red flowers and incense. Then, sitting there and reciting the mantra, one should summon [the desired person] by means of that skull-cup.
When the skull-cup moves, then one becomes accomplished.

Whomever one draws toward oneself with a finger, that person comes and performs all those tasks. One who desires to effect pacification should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times before the cloth painting;
thereafter, the painting will move.
Or, the image of the Tathāgata may move; thus, the accomplishment of the rite occurs. One should consecrate a blue cloth with one hundred and eight recitations and tie it into a knot.
The wrestler shall be victorious.
If ashes consecrated twenty-one times are applied to the wrestler's head,
he shall be victorious in battle.

Beginning from the first day of the bright fortnight, one should place [the medicine] together with ghee and milk in a copper vessel before the cloth painting, recite the mantra one hundred and eight times, and drink it for seven days;
one will become a possessor of the power of hearing (śrutidhara).
This occurs if a ray of light issues forth from the mudrā of the noble Mañjuśrī.
Having circumambulated it clockwise together with its receptacle, one ascends;
one becomes a vidyādhara,
able to assume any form at will and unimpeded, and lives for three thousand years.

Having fasted for a day and night on the eighth day of the dark fortnight and having become fearless, one should then strike a lion with a [mantra-empowered] blade consecrated seven times by a Vidyādhara.
Thereupon, the lion lets out a lion’s roar,
and the practitioner becomes motionless.
The wise one becomes ready within the interval of a nālikā;
then the practitioner should recite the mantra seven times,
and thereafter mount the lion.
All the vidyādharas assemble;
he who has a lion as his vehicle rises up together with his retinue,
moving with the speed of thought or the wind, surrounded by many vidyādharas, and remaining for an eon.
When one dies, one is reborn wherever one desires.
The Lion Sadhana:

Furthermore, one who desires to perform the Lion Sadhana should, on the full moon of the bright fortnight, observe absolute silence and subsist on milk and barley gruel until the next full moon, reciting the mantra one hundred thousand times.
Remaining silent and observing the *poṣadha* vows, he should take wood struck by a thunderbolt and soak it in milk for seven days.
Then, having taken white clay mixed with sandalwood water, one should bathe a piece of wood struck by a thunderbolt.

Thereafter, the practitioner should have a lion fashioned by a goldsmith who observes the *poṣadha* vows. Then, under the Puṣya asterism, having performed a magnificent worship of the Three Jewels, one should feed the monks designated for the Saṅgha.

Having performed an extensive worship before the cloth painting and offered various oblations (*bali*), the practitioner—pure and dressed in clean garments—should sit upon a bundle of *kuśa* grass. Grasping a lion with his right hand, he should recite the mantra until it moves like a lion.
When it moves, various kinds of signs arise;
then, an offering of water (*argha*) should be presented.
Furthermore, one should recite it one hundred and eight times;
mustard seeds will then come forth.
While reciting the mantra, a lion should be touched.
She becomes a woman;
she says,
"What shall I do?"
She should be told, "Enter within the body.
Then she disappears into the palm of the practitioner's hand;
at that very moment, he becomes one with curly locks of hair, appearing sixteen years of age, possessing a radiance like the rising sun, holding a spear in his hand, and moving with unimpeded gait.
Having seen her, he flies up together with them;
all the vidyādharas become subject to his command,
and he remains for an eon.
When he dies, he is reborn among the gods.

Having performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*), having installed the cloth painting in a reliquary shrine (*caitya*) containing relics, and subsequently placing it within his mouth, he becomes invisible;
he lives for a thousand years.

Having performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*) and subsisting on a diet of milk and barley-gruel, one should install the cloth-painting (*paṭa*) on a mountain peak, worship it with perfumes, flowers, and incense, and recite the mantra three hundred thousand times. Then, having taken ashes and earth from an anthill while observing the *poṣadha* vows, one should mix them with milk and knead them together. A peacock, measuring one span of a Sugata, should then be painted by a painter observing the *poṣadha* vows using colors that do not require animal glue.

Having gone to a secluded place, having installed the cloth painting (*paṭa*), having worshipped it with perfumes, flowers, and incense, and having offered a *bali* sacrifice for all beings, one who is pure and dressed in clean garments should then place a peacock before the painting and recite the mantra until the peacock moves.

Then, the *vidyādhara*, holding with his right hand a vessel containing the *aparājita* flowers previously consecrated by the root-mantra, should recite it until the sound of a jackal’s howl is heard.
While reciting the mantra, he should place living beings into his own mouth from among his companions and thus become invisible.
Having obtained all the siddhis, one lives for two thousand years.
One should grind together the filaments of a lotus, *sauvīra* collyrium, and *śilājatu*, making them into a paste, and have it ground by the hand of a girl observing the *poṣadha* vows.

Having encased it in the three metals and performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*), one should, under the conjunction of the Puṣya asterism, perform worship with perfumes, flowers, and incense, offering a *bali* consisting of all kinds of ingredients before an image of Maheśvara. Placing it in a casket made of two earthenware bowls and pressing it with the right hand, one should recite the mantra until it makes a clattering sound (*khaṭakhaṭāyati*).

Having offered one [portion] to the Blessed One and distributed [the rest] among his companions, he himself should offer ten thousand oblations of *apāmārga* fuel-sticks smeared with curd, honey, and clarified butter.
He will obtain ten thousand pieces of gold.

Taking bamboo-resin (*vaṃśarocanā*), he should fashion pills encased in three metals; then, having gone to a cremation ground dressed in pure white garments, having performed worship with perfumes, flowers, and incense, and having offered a bali-oblation to all spirits, he should place the pills within a hollowed skull-cup and recite the mantra until the sound of "kilakila" is heard.
One should not be afraid. Even by separating [the mantra] from its companions and placing it within one's own mouth, one becomes invisible and lives for ten thousand years.
Taking an owl’s eye together with ointment, one should grind it in the hand of a young girl.

Having encased it in three metals and placed the pill within a pair of earthenware bowls, one who observes silence regarding wood for six months and recites the mantra before an image of Maheśvara worthy of offerings for seven nights will attract a yakṣiṇī.
One obtains the desired object.

Having fashioned an image of King Arka six finger-breadths in height from clay that does not stick together, and having painted it with non-adhesive pigments, adorned with all ornaments, one should recite the mantra before it for six months;
one will obtain a regional kingdom.
Or one may attain the state of a Vidyādhara.
Remaining silent before the cloth painting for six months, having consecrated the palm of the left hand and recited the mantra ten thousand times, one obtains a well-concealed treasure.
Having descended to a river flowing to the ocean, one should offer ten thousand oblations of Arka flowers smeared with curd, honey, and ghee into an Arka leaf-cup.
Āditya becomes a granter of boons.
Having descended into that very river with water reaching only to the waist, one should cause sesame seeds and flowers to float away;
Pitāmaha becomes a granter of boons.
One should offer oblations of *mandāra* flowers;
Śakra becomes a granter of boons.
In that very water, with *mandāra* flowers, Dhanada becomes a granter of boons.
By reciting the mantra two hundred thousand times, one attracts a king;
by reciting it three hundred thousand times, one attracts all sentient beings.
Having descended to a river that flows to the ocean, one should offer ten thousand *aśoka* flowers as a burnt oblation.

Having performed an extensive worship before the original cloth painting, one should place a wheel or a swastika upon an aśvattha leaf and, sitting in the paryaṅka posture, recite the mantra until it blazes.
By merely grasping it, one becomes a universal monarch of the vidyādharas with curly, ringed hair and a complexion like the rising sun;
and together with those who see him and those whom he sees, he flies up into the air.
Having taken the root of the *sudarśana* plant and holding it in one's hand, one should recite the mantra a thousand times; then, having tied it to the hand, whomever one touches becomes submissive.
Having taken a wheel made of *kuśa* grass and recited the mantra a thousand times, one should cast it into water; then a *nāga* emerges and says, "What shall I do?"
One should say, "Give me one hundred thousand.
Having subsisted on alms-food, one should ascend a mountain peak and recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times;
then the forms of the Tathāgatas will appear before one's eyes.
Upon seeing her, whatever one seeks to accomplish is achieved;
women appear adorned with every ornament,
and men who honor the Buddha attend simultaneously with laughter, dance, and other such gestures.
Whatever one thinks of, all that comes to pass.
At dawn, having extracted it, everything perishes.

Beginning from the first day of the bright fortnight, having fasted for a day and night, one should recite the mantra eight hundred times over a *karṣa* of *brahmī*, a *karṣa* of cow’s ghee, and a *karṣa* of milk before the cloth painting, and drink it for seven days.
One becomes a possessor of a retentive memory.
Having placed various kinds of food and edibles before the cloth painting, one should recite the mantra until the food has vanished;
thereafter, the food is transferred [to oneself].
And [the ritual involves] varieties of rice.

Having performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*), one should fashion a sixteen-spoked wheel out of the three metals (*triloha*). On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, having fasted for a day and night, one should perform worship at a crossroads and sit down. Placing a piece of realgar (*manaḥśilā*) the size of a *kalāpa* in the mouth, one should recite the mantra until the mouth bursts open. The realgar becomes perfected (*siddha*).
Having applied a *tilaka*, one becomes invisible, able to assume any form at will, and lives for five hundred years.
On the eighth day of the dark fortnight, one should have a couch, a courtesan, and a trident fashioned.

On the following eighth day of the dark fortnight, having fasted for a day and night, one should go to a cremation ground and perform a great worship of the trident. Seated in the *paryaṅka* posture and grasping the trident with the right hand, one should recite the mantra until a ray of light issues forth from the trident.
Then one becomes successful.
If one buries [the image] at night, a divine house is produced.

Having installed the cloth painting (*paṭa*) in a pure place and fasted for a day and a night, one should fashion a small figure (*puttalikā*) before the painting and, having worshipped it according to the ritual rules, offer eight thousand oblations of *bilva* wood fuel sticks smeared with curd, honey, and ghee.
A ray of light issues forth from the forehead of the Blessed Mañjuśrī;
from that, one becomes accomplished and obtains immeasurable gold and wealth.

Having fasted for a day and night, one should take a single *karavīra* flower before the cloth painting, go to a place where *nāgas* dwell, and cast the flower into a *nāga* pool while reciting the mantra.
The *nāgas* and *nāginīs* will become submissive; whatever one requests, that one shall obtain.

Having performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*) and fasted for a day and night, one who desires to destroy fever should offer eight thousand oblations of *girikarṇikā* flowers on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight;
the fevers caused by *piśācas* will be destroyed.
By offering one hundred and eight oblations of *khadira* wood fuel-sticks, one causes all planetary spirits (*graha*) to release their hold.
The Lord of Mantras binds the supreme mantras with ashes over which the mantra has been recited seven times;
liberation occurs through water over which it has been recited once.
Having written [the mantra] on cloth or birch bark, one should fasten it to the top of a banner.
The enemy army becomes paralyzed.

One who subsists on water and barley-meal, having fasted for three nights on either the eighth or the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, should go to a solitary linga. Placing his right foot upon the top of the linga, he should bind it with *vālaśolaka* grass. Having clenched his fist, he should recite the mantra until the sound "I am dying" emerges.
On the third night, the fist becomes empowered (*siddha*).
Having formed a fist, one lives for seven hundred years;
so too does one become a member of Maheśvara’s retinue.
With *gorocanā* consecrated a thousand times, whatever mark one applies, whoever sees it [is affected].
All become submissive.
Having risen in the morning, having consecrated water seven times with mantras and washed one's face, whoever one gives a look to becomes submissive.
Likewise, for one desiring food, one should consecrate a handful of water seven times with mantras and drink it along with oil.
One obtains food without having asked for it.
When entering a royal court, one should take a corner of one's robe, recite the mantra twenty-one times over it, and tie a knot with the left hand; thus, one becomes possessed of unimpeded speech.
This should be remembered when in the midst of thieves.
And one releases those who are bound.

For mantras that have been cut, broken, or overused, one should fashion an image out of *śāli* rice, *vrīhi* rice, white *karavīra*, and white mustard seeds; holding it with the left hand in front of the cloth painting, one should recite the mantra eight thousand times.
Thus, the restoration of the mantras is accomplished.
One obtains a thousand cows.
By burning ghee and resin of the *sarja* tree according to this very procedure, one should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times;
one then obtains twelve excellent villages.
Having constructed a stūpa according to this very procedure, one should offer one hundred thousand lotuses anointed with sandalwood;
one will obtain sovereignty over a country. Having constructed a stūpa measuring one span of a Sugata, while burning incense, one should offer one hundred thousand campaka flowers.

One obtains a thousand pieces of gold. Having constructed a stūpa the size of a Sugata’s span, or having painted an image of it, one should stand upon it with the left foot and recite the mantra eight thousand times;
thus, [the target] comes under control by their very lineage.
Having constructed a stūpa measuring one Sugata-span, one should offer eight thousand oblations of wedding parched grains (*lāja*) smeared with curd, honey, and ghee into the fire.
With the ashes, one should perform the binding of a protective circle (*maṇḍalabandha*).

Having bathed at dawn, one should churn butter using this very mantra, take it, perform a grand worship, and while burning incense, consume it—having consecrated it eight thousand times—without touching it with the teeth.
By whose name he [the practitioner] gains control over that person—
provided it is not connected with sensual desire—

one who has fasted for three nights, having performed a grand worship of the cloth painting with all kinds of perfumes purchased by a hero’s sale, and having lit a lamp of ghee, should himself recite the mantra.
Having made a doll from that [powder] and placed it upon seven *aśvattha* leaves, one should recite the mantra until it becomes supple.
Having turned that into powder, whoever is touched by it becomes submissive.
By this very same procedure, [one may act] with the powder of *nāgakeśara*.
Having fashioned an image, one should offer oblations one hundred and eight times into incense burners;
whoever one contemplates shall be brought under one's control.
By this very same procedure, one should offer oblations of *apāmārga* wood.

One who desires wealth should go to a cow-pen, fashion a stūpa one cubit high out of fallen cow dung before a painted image, worship it according to the ritual rules while burning guggulu incense, and recite the mantra one hundred thousand times.
He will become invincible to all *vidyādharas* and shall travel through the paths of the seven winds.

Taking the index finger of one who has not yet reached the age of one year, one should fashion a hand-sized caitya and perform a ritual worship according to the rules in a cremation ground. Seated facing east upon a bed of *kuśa* grass, one should offer that finger and press down with the [other] index finger, reciting the mantra until a ray of light issues forth and the flame of the lamp increases.
Having performed the protection rites and taken hold of that kingdom, whoever one draws toward oneself with that finger at dawn becomes submissive.

Having fasted for three nights, one should take the milk of a milch cow that has a calf of the same color; having prepared a mandala before the cloth painting and lit a lamp of ghee, one should place the milk in an earthen vessel after it has been consecrated eight thousand times while resting upon a bed of *kuśa* grass.
A fire-oblation (*homa*) to Vināyaka should be performed with curd, honey, and ghee.

Then, having prepared a mandala and stationed the guardians of the four directions, the awakener—holding mustard seeds in his hand—should be in the second mandala, while a good assistant is in the third. Having performed a great worship and established the protection, he should sit facing east and, grasping [the object] with his hand, recite the mantra until it emits heat, smoke, and flame.
By the first [attainment], one whose eyes are anointed becomes such that everyone whom he looks upon and who looks upon him all become subject to his will.
By the second [attainment], having achieved success, he possesses the strength of nine thousand nāgas, has the speed of the wind, and lives for five thousand years.

One becomes an invincible master of all vidyās. If eight thousand recitations are performed over an invisibility potion, it will blaze with the color of the rising sun; one whose body is adorned with jewels shall remain for the duration of an eon. Having consecrated [the substance] eight thousand times, if one enters the midst of enemies, no fear shall arise, and one shall be invulnerable to all foes.

For possession, one uses white flowers; for making [the deity] dance, one uses water over which the mantra has been recited three times; with karavīra flowers over which the mantra has been recited three times, one may summon [the deity].
He speaks of the past and the future.
Binding is [effected] by a snap of the fingers; cutting is [effected] by the same.

One desiring to accomplish the collyrium (*añjana*) should take *sauvīra* collyrium purchased from a hero, remove the insects, and grind it with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*) using a mortar facing north.
Having formed four pills with the ring finger and covered them with a lotus leaf, one should let them dry.

Having lit a fire according to the ritual rules in front of the cloth painting (*paṭa*), having performed a thousand oblations (*sampātāhuti*), and having made a grand offering at a reliquary (*caitya*) containing relics, one should kindle the fire with *palāśa* wood from the eight directions and place it within the waist-belt.
Thus, the binding of semen (*śukrabandha*) is accomplished.
Having tied a knot with the corner of a robe-cloth over which the mantra has been recited seven times, there is the binding of poison;
it is also the treatment for poison. By means of a sprout and the breaking of the seal, one effects possession through water.
A binding of the seizing spirits (*graha*) is effected by means of *guggulu* incense or water.
Having consecrated one's finger with the mantra, whomever one threatens becomes submissive.
One should recite the mantra one hundred and eight times before the cloth painting (*paṭa*).
It reveals things as they truly are in a dream.

Having installed a cloth painting in a reliquary containing relics, having performed extensive worship before it, and having kindled a fire with *bilva* wood, one should offer a hundred thousand oblations of white lotuses smeared with curd, honey, and ghee.
One will obtain a kingdom.
If [the rite] is not successful, one obtains a village with a thousand households.
Alternatively, one should recite the mantra a thousand times before a cloth painting while holding *gorocanā* or *manaḥśilā*.
Having applied a mark (*tilaka*) made from that, whatever one seeks, one obtains it.
On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, having fasted for one night, one should offer eight thousand oblations at night into a fire made from the root of a *paṭaka* tree and *kāṃsāra* wood;
one will obtain a thousand gold coins (*rūpaka*).
On the eighth day of the bright fortnight, having fasted for a full day and night, one should descend to a river flowing to the ocean and offer ten thousand lotuses.
One obtains a kingdom.

For the subjugation of men, having fasted for one night on the eighth day of the dark fortnight, one should kindle a fire with wood from the Bodhi tree and offer eight thousand water lilies smeared with curd, honey, and ghee;
he becomes submissive.

For the subjugation of women, one should strike Ārya Mañjuśrī with *saugandhika* flowers on the twelfth day of the dark fortnight. With the intent of binding medicinal herbs, it serves as a means for driving away bipeds and quadrupeds;
it bestows five *dīnāras* every single day.
It should be spent entirely for the sake of making offerings to the Three Jewels;
one should recite the mantra for one month before the cloth painting.
One obtains twelve thousand dīnāras.
Beginning from the eighth day of the bright fortnight, one should recite the mantra for six months at a shrine containing relics;
[the deity] bestows a kingdom.
On the eighth day of the dark fortnight, having fasted for a full day and night, one should take a bud of the *śleṣmātaka* tree before a painted image and wrap it with red thread.

Then, having kindled a fire with *palāśa* wood and consecrated a ritual stake (*kīlaka*) eight thousand times, one should recite the mantra twenty-one times over each individual fragment and cast them into the fire. At dawn, one obtains hundreds of *dīnāra* coins. On the eighth day of the bright fortnight, having fasted for one night, one should offer eight thousand *atimuktaka* flowers for seven days.
One obtains a hundred dīnāras.
By anointing the eyes with [a substance] consecrated seven times,
one becomes beloved by all people.

Having consecrated common collyrium with mantras, whoever one first sees becomes subject to one's will. Reciting [the mantra] ten thousand times before a painted cloth (paṭa) while focusing on a specific person,
or reciting it one hundred thousand times at the entrance of a cave, [achieves the same].

Just as prescribed, having established a reliquary stūpa containing the *pratītyasamutpāda* formula on a mountain peak or in a cow-pen, one should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times; one will obtain one hundred thousand *dīnāras*.

Having established the painted cloth (*paṭa*) at a site of the *nāgas* and performed the ritual of protection well, one should kindle a fire with *jambuka* wood, offer a sacrificial oblation (*bali*) of the "three sweets," and perform eight thousand burnt offerings (*homa*) of *nāgapuṣpa* flowers.
Thereupon, the *nāga* king, appearing in the form of a Brahmin, arrives.
And he says:
"You must say, 'Give seven dinars every day.
Having said, 'So be it,' he becomes invisible."
For the subjugation of a general, one should smear a large mandala, take the dust from his feet, and offer a thousand oblations with the left hand;
he will become submissive.
For the subjugation of an ordinary woman, one should fashion an image out of salt, cut it into pieces, and offer them as oblations with the left hand.
One becomes submissive.
Furthermore, for the subjugation of a female slave, one should combine *punnāga* filaments, barley, and wheat, and offer them into the fire eight thousand times;
she will become submissive.
Having fashioned an image out of rice flour and cutting it into pieces again and again, one should offer them as oblations;
[the target] becomes submissive.
For the subjugation of a widow, one should offer oblations of *māṣa* and *jambūlika*.
One becomes subject to one's will.

If one takes *śrotāñjana* (antimony), places it between two leaves of the *aśvattha* tree at a single shrine, and consecrates it eight thousand times, if one performs the practice again, one’s lifespan becomes doubled.
Having entered a granary and established the cloth-painting (*paṭa*) in a clean place, one should recite the mantra for one fortnight while observing silence and subsisting on milk and barley-gruel.

Then, having performed a magnificent worship of the cloth painting and having offered a most magnificent *bali* offering, one should sit in the cross-legged posture (*paryaṅka*) and recite the mantra until rays of light emerge.
Upon seeing them, even the five sins of immediate retribution (*pañcānantarya*) go to destruction.
Thereafter, one becomes accomplished (*siddha*).
One obtains great sovereignty and becomes free from adversaries.
Having consecrated bezoar eight thousand times with mantras and fumigated it with incense, one should place it between the teeth.
One becomes a superior debater,
and all become subject to one's will.
On the eighth day of the bright fortnight, having fasted for three nights, one should recite the mantra eight thousand times before the painted image.
One obtains a single dīnāra.

Having fasted for three nights before the cloth painting on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight, while burning guggulu incense and kindling a fire of strength, one should offer eight thousand karavīra flowers smeared with curd, honey, and ghee.
Then, in the fire-pit which is the size of a lotus, one sees a substance resembling karavīra and realgar.
While reciting the mantra, one should grasp it.
Having been grasped by her, one becomes a Vidyadhara with the complexion of the rising sun and the appearance of a sixteen-year-old;
through a state of equality with the wind, most desired foods arise.
He lives for eighty thousand years;
he is inaccessible to all beings and brings about death.
One should perform the rite before a cloth painting; by casting it into one's mouth, one becomes invisible.
First, the release from bondage must be performed:

having fashioned an image out of honey and beeswax, whether of a woman or a man, one should kindle a fire in a secluded place and, having consecrated it with mantras, cause it to be offered as an oblation.
Having pierced [the target] one hundred and eight times with a *madanakaṇṭaka* thorn, one should cause [it] to be given;
they become submissive,
and whatever one prays for, that one obtains.
On the full moon day of the bright fortnight, having fasted for a day and night, one should offer eight hundred fragrant flowers;
one will obtain five *kārsāpaṇa* coins.

On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, having fasted for a day and night, one should kindle a fire before the cloth painting with *priyaṅgu* wood and offer eight thousand oblations of *vaikaṅkata* fuel sticks.
By reciting [the mantra] one hundred times over it, all piercing pain is pacified.
For a woman experiencing difficult labor, water should be consecrated by reciting [the mantra] eight hundred times and given to her;
she will give birth with ease.
Beginning from the first day of the bright fortnight, one should recite [the mantra] with an increase of one thousand each day until the fifteenth day.
At the conclusion, having fasted for three nights and having prepared a pill by means of the *guḍikā*-yoga and empowered it, one should place it in the mouth and become invisible.

One should take blue *aśoka* flowers, the bile of a black antelope, and the heart of a ruddy goose (*cakravāka*), together with the fat of a Vedic scholar (*śrotriya*); these should be mixed in equal parts and wrapped in "flower-metal" (*puṣpaloha*).

Having further wrapped it in the three metals, one who desires to accomplish the rite should place it before a statue containing relics and likewise install the painted cloth there. On the eighth day of the bright fortnight, having performed worship and placed the substance upon seven *aśvattha* leaves, one should prepare a mandala. In the center of that, having placed a man whose limbs are uninjured, one should step upon his chest with the left foot; then, having performed the protection rites, one should recite the mantra until [the figure] rises as before.
Then one should feed him honeyed milk-rice.
Having formed a handful [of the rice] consecrated seven times, it should be struck upon his head;
then he vomits.
Having drunk it, he becomes invisible.
Having fasted for three nights, one should descend into water reaching up to the navel during a lunar eclipse and recite the mantra until the moon is released;
one then obtains one hundred dīnāras.
One should cause it to revolve and obtain auspiciousness.
Having bathed with water mixed with salt and performed anointment, and having worshipped with perfumes and garlands, one should feed the previously prepared milk-rice (*pāyasa*).
Having recited the mantra seven times over a handful [of the rice], it should be struck upon the head.
Then he vomits it up;
having eaten that, one becomes a vidyādhara who remains for a great kalpa.
Having empowered a weapon with one hundred and eight recitations, one should strike [the enemy] after cutting and splitting it.
The gold becomes capable of piercing a thousand times.
Having performed the purification of the body, one should construct a caitya with one's own hands;
even one who has committed the five acts of immediate retribution attains success.
By means of a hundred thousand *caityas*, one becomes a universal monarch (*cakravartin*) of the *vidyādharas*.

He is proficient in all treatises (*śāstra*), endowed with all specialized knowledge (*vijñāna*), and remains for an eon (*kalpa*). Even after passing away, he does not go to the states of woe for five hundred births.
He is born in the most exalted central regions, possessed of all sense faculties, a retainer of what he has heard, and one who remembers his past lives.
Having obtained red arsenic (manaḥśilā) without asking for it, one should place it upon seven leaves of the holy fig tree (aśvattha) and perform the rite.
All those who hear or smell it at twilight become submissive.
It emerges, piercing through mountains, walls, and the ocean.

In a cremation ground, having smeared a mandala measuring sixteen or eight cubits, one should place a corpse with its head toward the north, insert a finger into its mouth, and step upon its chest with the right foot. One should recite the mantra until the corpse moves;
then, grasping that finger with the hand, one gives it [to the deity].
Having inserted it into the ring finger, whoever one commands by means of the *yamākāra* gesture arrives.
Saying "Return!", he causes [the corpse] to return.
Having placed his foot upon the chest of a corpse whose limbs are unimpaired, he should recite the mantra until the corpse rises.

Having prepared a mantra there by writing it with saffron on the eighth or fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, being observant of the *poṣadha* vows and established in the precepts, one should go alone—without anyone else—to a mountain peak. Having avoided the guardians of the directions, having smeared a mandala eight cubits in size, and having fashioned a stupa made of sand, one should perform worship according to one's ability. Facing east, holding a sword in the right hand with the arm raised, one should recite the mantra in front of the stupa until the syllables have vanished.
Having taken that leaf, which has become like a sword and is blazing, one becomes a *vidyādhara* who travels at will;

he is invulnerable to all *vidyādharas* and unassailable by all beings. He can assume any form at will, remain for an eon (*kalpa*), and see for a thousand *yojanas*. With reed leaves smeared with pungent oil, there is the pacification of *māras*; with rice grains from a mountain-field, there is prosperity; and with mustard seeds over which the mantra has been recited one hundred thousand times, one destroys the mantras of the *asuras*.
With an arrow over which the mantra has been recited eight hundred times, one causes thunderbolts, diamonds, stones, and the like to fall wherever one desires.
With ashes over which it has been recited seven times, in whichever direction one scatters them, there a protection against arrows is established.
With [ashes] over which it has been recited eight hundred times, all arrows are extracted.
Having performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*), one should recite [the mantra] twenty-five hundred thousand times before the painted image (*paṭa*).

Then, having consecrated a fingernail-scraper, a palm leaf, a sword, a protection for all crops, or a substance to be licked—intended for bipeds, quadrupeds, insects, mice, and so forth—with eight thousand recitations, one should cast it into water.
One becomes invulnerable to all *nāgas*.
By reciting the mantra one hundred thousand times, one releases from bondage whomever one desires.
During a solar eclipse, having placed the ghee of a cow that has a calf of the same age into a copper vessel, one should recite the mantra until the sun is released.
By drinking that [ghee], one is freed from all diseases.

Following the previously described procedure, one who observes the *poṣadha* vows should offer one hundred thousand oblations of *śrīpiṣṭa* mixed with resin (*sarjarasa*) into a reliquary containing relics.
One will obtain a thousand *dīnāras*.
One should offer eight thousand oblations of white mustard seeds smeared with clarified butter.
Then she reveals the treasure;
it should be taken.

Having constructed a stūpa the size of a Sugata’s span, containing the essence of dependent origination (*pratītyasamutpāda*), made of sand at a stūpa containing relics or by a river flowing to the ocean, one who is pure and observing the *poṣadha* vows should perform worship according to one's ability, subsisting on alms-food or sacrificial food (*haviṣya*), and recite the mantra one hundred thousand times.
One becomes capable of all ritual actions (*sarvakarmasamartha*).

By gathering [substances] from a great cremation ground (*mahāśmaśāna*), there is the binding of the cardinal and intermediate directions of the mandala and so forth; it effects the healing of all poisons, the cleansing [of afflictions], and the destruction of seizures and fevers.
One should recite the mantra when crossing a great river.
One crosses over with ease;
by mere recitation, one becomes honored by ferrymen, customs officers, forest guards, and others;
and in a dispute, one becomes the respondent.

With a thousand recitations of the mantra over *nidrā*, semen, and urine, and with eight thousand recitations over stakes of *khadira* wood, one cannot be brought under the power of another's mantra. Furthermore, having made an image of butter the size of a thumb-joint from barley grains smeared with curd, honey, and ghee, and having placed it upon an *aśvattha* leaf, one should press it with the hand and recite the mantra until it quivers; then, one should seize it without touching it with the teeth.
At that very moment, she arrives in beautiful form;
she becomes the granter of all desires.
Having kindled a fire with *bilva* wood, one should offer ten thousand oblations of *bilva* fuel-sticks.

One obtains enjoyments; in all ritual procedures, there is the binding of a circle, the binding of a boundary, and the binding of the mouth against thieves, tigers, crocodiles, sharks, and water-monsters,
as well as the seizing of hidden treasures.
Having gone to the place where the ritual injunction is located, one should fast there, smear a mandala, kindle a fire with wood from the *bilva* tree, and offer royal mustard seeds as oblations;
one will obtain a treasure-trove.
If one desires to bring under control the queen together with her retinue, one should fashion an image out of *kuśa* grass, grasp it with the left hand, and recite the mantra a thousand times.
She becomes submissive along with her retinue.
To subjugate a brahmin, one should offer eight thousand oblations of sesame seeds smeared with curd, honey, and ghee; he will become submissive along with his retinue.
To subjugate a kṣatriya, one should offer eight thousand oblations of barley with curd, honey, and ghee.
He becomes submissive along with his retinue.
For the subjugation of a Vaiśya, one should offer eight thousand oblations of black mustard seeds;
he becomes submissive along with his retinue.
To bring a Śūdra under one's control, one should offer eight thousand husks of black rice;
he becomes submissive.
The oblation should be performed alone for three days.
Having combined the ghee of that very Kapilā cow with *mālatī* flowers, one should offer seven oblations.
If one places white mustard seeds consecrated seven times upon someone's head, that person becomes submissive.
For the subjugation of a king, having fashioned an image of him, one should step upon it with the left hand and recite the mantra eight thousand times.
One becomes a master over them along with their retinue.
Having consecrated well-strained water, one should keep it for seven days.
Then, having performed the protection rite, one should have a cow milked by a cowherd.
Then, one should recite mantras over that milk in a secluded place while it is in a jar.
Having stirred it, one should have a Brahmin girl grind lotus seeds, *tagara*, lotus filaments, and sandalwood together with honey.
Having formed this into a pill and consecrated it with mantras, whoever one gives it to along with betel leaf becomes submissive.
Having recited the mantra over a garland of flowers, whoever one gives it upon their head becomes submissive.

One should take red sandalwood, *campaka* flowers, lotus filaments, the husks of red *śāli* rice, *girikarṇikā*, seeds of *koraṇḍaka*, rice, black gram, *kuṣṭha*, *tagara*, and *turuṣka* oil; having combined these, one should have them made into equal portions.
Having kindled a fire with *jāti* wood, one should offer eight thousand oblations of *jāti* flowers smeared with curd, honey, and ghee.
One obtains five hundred dīnāras.
Having kindled a fire with mango wood on a riverbank, one should offer eight thousand oblations of *arka* fuel-sticks smeared with curd, honey, and ghee.
On the fifth day, one obtains five dīnāras.
Beginning on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight and continuing until the fifteenth, one should offer eight thousand oblations of *aśoka* wood fuel smeared with curd, honey, and ghee;
one will obtain one hundred *dīnāras*.
Having kindled a fire with *karavīra* wood, one should offer eight thousand oblations of *karavīra* creepers.
Beginning from the eighth day of the bright fortnight until the fourteenth, one obtains a thousand dīnāras every day; one should offer oblations eight thousand times daily until the fourteenth.
By this, even a royal family that has become angry due to many actions is appeased like a friend.

One who has completed the preparatory rites (*puraścaraṇa*) should take a piece of wood six finger-breadths long from a tree struck by lightning. Having fasted for three nights, he should install a cloth painting in a reliquary stūpa containing relics. He should bind that ritual stake (*kīlaka*) with the three metals and place four jars filled with all medicinal herbs upon a bed of lotuses.
Treading upon that stake with his left foot and grasping it with his left hand, he should recite the mantra until it vanishes; even when it is gone, he must not let go of his hand.
Then one should offer a great bali-oblation;
at dawn, one should eat a pomegranate.
Thus that stake becomes accomplished.
If one buries it in the forest, it becomes a house that grants all desires; all necessary utensils and provisions appear there.
Once it has been unearthed, everyone who drinks from it and bathes therein shall again possess this same ritual efficacy.
This shall continue throughout the entire night.
At dawn, the monks designated by the Saṃgha are to be fed;
having fed them, one should eat pomegranates accompanied by ghee.
He approaches;
the fourteen branches of knowledge enter his mouth;
he is one who retains what he has heard.
Having descended to a river flowing to the ocean, one should form a fist with the right hand and recite the mantra for thirteen days;
it raises up all those bitten by venomous creatures and destroys all seizing spirits (grahas) with that fist.
Being released by his own will,
having stayed for three nights beneath an *aśoka* tree, he should offer eight thousand oblations of black pepper (*marīca*).
Having placed a single grain of black pepper in his mouth, he should gaze at Yama without blinking.
He gazes upon it and gains mastery over it;
by mere recollection, he destroys all calamities.
If there is a woman who does not please him, one should take her name, recite the mantra over clarified butter (*ghṛta*), and have it given to her.
One becomes fortunate.
This is the Vajra-attainment (*vajrasādhana*).

Having fashioned a vajra out of *puṣpaloha* iron, sixteen finger-breadths long and with three prongs, one should descend into a river flowing to the ocean and offer one hundred thousand fragrant flowers.
The western flower comes forth, piercing against the current;
one should swallow it without touching it with the teeth. Day by day, one grasps five hundred knots.
Having performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*), one should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times before the cloth painting.
Then, having gone to the place where the treasure is located, one should smear a jar made of *kālamūla* wood with all kinds of perfumes and fill it with water mixed with white sandalwood.
Having consecrated it eight thousand times, one should place it at the site of the treasure.
The entire ground trembles;
a treasure remains at the height of a man;
it should be seized.
One should offer one hundred thousand fuel-sticks of *palāśa*;
one obtains a thousand cows.
One should offer one hundred thousand *śephālikā* flowers.
One obtains the desired object.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of *arka* wood fuel;
one obtains a thousand *dīnāra*s.
One should offer oblations of fresh butter;
one obtains five villages.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of *piṇḍāraka* flowers.
One obtains forty million pieces of fine cloth;
one should offer a hundred thousand oblations of milk,
and one obtains a hundred garments of *vitarka* silk.
One should offer a hundred thousand *kumuda* flowers;
one obtains a wife together with gold.
One should offer a hundred thousand *piṇḍāraka* flowers.
Having ascended a mountain peak, one should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times.
In whatever region one performs the recitation, the king of that region will attend upon one as a son.
One should offer oblations of lotuses marked with the syllable Śrī.
Padmaśrī comes;
one who desires victory should constantly offer curd as an oblation,
and constant victory shall prevail.
One desiring nourishment should offer oblations of clarified butter;
the attainment of wealth will occur.

One who is pure should perform this constantly: for five nights [to influence] a king, for seven nights [to influence] piśācas, for nine nights [to influence] yakṣas and rākṣasas, for twelve nights [to influence] the kings of the nāgas, for half a month [to influence] gandharvas and apsarases, for twenty-one days [to influence] gods, dānavas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and divine beings, and for twenty-four nights [to influence] all the hosts. To subjugate the wife of a king, one should offer eight thousand oblations of *asurasamañjarī*, curd, honey, and clarified butter.
She becomes submissive.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of red karavīra buds;
one obtains a princess.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of bilva fruits smeared with bilva oil;
prosperity will arise in the house.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of śatapuṣpā flowers smeared with curd.
One obtains a hundred dīnāras.
Having empowered eight thousand pieces of black salt (*sauvarcala*) with the mantra, one who has anointed their eyes with it brings all sentient beings under control.
Having recited the mantra over perfumes, one should apply them.
The subjugation of all beings:
having recited the mantra over one's own form, one should fumigate oneself; this is the subjugation of all beings.
Having recited the mantra over the topknot, one should bind it.
Protection everywhere;
the immobilization of all beings;
for one who desires to bring a widow under control.
One should offer oblations of black gram (māṣa);
all beings will become submissive.
If one desires to bring a yakṣiṇī under control, one should offer eight thousand lotuses.
She arrives within three nights;
if she does not arrive then, she arrives within seven nights,
and she becomes a granter of boons.
One should seek according to one's desire.
One who desires a maiden should offer a hundred thousand oblations;
he obtains the maiden he desires.

Then, desiring to accomplish the rite of the Vetāla, one should take a corpse with its limbs unbroken to a cremation ground, or to a place with a single tree, or a crossroads, or a solitary linga. Having presented an offering to all the spirits (*sarvabhūtika*) and having smeared a mandala before the southern form of Mahādeva and offered the oblation, one should bathe and adorn [the corpse]. Having drawn a mandala with ashes, one should place it there with the head facing east. The practitioner, covered by a white cloth, together with companions dressed in white garments, should station the guardians of the directions. Sitting upon a prepared seat, he should offer sesame and mustard seeds into the mouth of the corpse.
This continues until the jewel emerges from his mouth.

Having taken it and placed it in one's own mouth, and having offered a bali-oblation to all beings, one should stand before the right image. Taking a combination of yellow orpiment, realgar, collyrium, madder, and gorocanā, and having enclosed them between *aśvattha* leaves, one should recite the mantra until the threefold accomplishment occurs—namely, it becomes hot, emits smoke, and blazes.
When it becomes hot, one becomes a traveler on foot with a lifespan of five thousand years.
By means of this, one gains mastery over all sentient beings.
When [the smoke] begins to smolder, one becomes invisible and attains a lifespan of ten thousand years.
When it blazes into flame, one becomes a master of all vidyādharas.
The lord of all vidyādharas, remaining for the duration of a kalpa, becomes one endowed with the five superknowledges by reciting [the mantra] one hundred thousand times above the water.
He gains mastery over those bound above and below, as well as over the guardians of the directions,
and becomes most beloved in the royal court.
And he becomes one whose words are accepted.
One who desires a maiden should offer eight thousand *jāti* flowers;
he obtains a maiden.
By means of blossoming flowers, there is the attainment of women;
or by means of the seal of all planets, by speech, by a message, or by yellow pigment (rocanā), one paralyzes fire and paralyzes ships.
It draws in those who have been bitten or those who have not; it causes possession;
it raises the dead;
and by means of speech, it sends away fever.

Subsisting on a diet of milk and barley-gruel, having fasted for three nights and wearing clean garments, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times. Having installed [the deity] within a *liṅga* containing the practitioner (*sādhaka-garbha*), and having performed a great worship, one should recite it an immeasurable number of times.
All children and the elderly will become submissive.
One may also fashion an armlet using ashes consecrated seven times with the mantra.
One should cause water empowered by reciting [the mantra] one hundred and eight times to be given to all beings;
it pacifies their diseases.

Having fasted for a day and night and fashioned a sword from *khadira* wood, one should recite [the mantra] in a cremation ground on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight until it blazes. By grasping that [sword], one becomes a *vidyādhara* with unimpeded movement, possessing a sword.
One whose hair is curled in ringlets, who remains for an eon, and is highly esteemed by all the Vidyādharas; or else,
having performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*) during an eclipse of the moon or sun, one should rise at dawn, perform worship of the cloth painting (*paṭa*), feed the monks,
and seek success (*siddhi*) together with ritual fees (*dakṣiṇā*).
Then one becomes successful in even more difficult rites.
One should offer eight thousand oblations of *dūrvā* sprouts smeared with curds, honey, and ghee;
this releases from bondage. Furthermore, having consecrated a sword eight thousand times with mantras, one should place it at the entrance of a cave, a temple, or a city gate.
Having broken the door-panel, he tears open the door.
With a single recitation, there is protection for oneself.
By offerings of milk, women become submissive.
With the mind, one establishes the two mantras;
one paralyzes all mudrās and pulverizes all mantras.
One brings an asura maiden under one's control.
By offering a hundred oblations of all types of fragrances, women of noble family become submissive.
By offering the remains of divine offerings (*devanirmālya*) into the fire, deities, temple attendants (*taṭika*), and renunciants become submissive.
Placing the hand upon the heart, one should recite;
this destroys all sins and attracts all sentient beings.
Placing the hand upon the head, one should recite.
One hundred and eight [times]:
this stuns all beings and destroys their sins.
Having recited over a *bilva* fruit, one attracts all beings.
In the practice of the *śikhā*, one should recite [the mantra] starting from the first day of the bright fortnight until the twilight.
Then, having consecrated the topknot (*śikhā*) with eight thousand recitations,
one should go for alms at the houses of Brahmins.
At that time, when the giver of alms does not see [the practitioner], then it becomes accomplished.
On the first day, there is one portion of alms;
and so on for seven days.
On the twenty-first day, it succeeds even for one who lacks merit.
During a lunar eclipse, having recited the mantra over milk, one should drink it; it becomes a great elixir (*rasāyana*).
Having recited the mantra twenty-one times over a handful of water, if one throws it toward the house of someone for seven days, that person becomes submissive.
Having consecrated a handful of water seven times with mantras, whoever drinks it while reciting the name of another becomes submissive.
Whoever looks at someone while their gaze has been empowered by recitation twenty-one times becomes submissive. By performing one hundred thousand oblations of *guggulu* resin, one obtains a kingdom.
By offering or burning blue lotuses, white water lilies, white lotuses, and so forth, one brings whoever one desires under control.
A wall of fire is broken by [the recitation over] broken [substances], or a protection of the hair-tuft (*śikhābandha*) is formed with pebbles in water.
Taking natural collyrium, one should apply it after reciting the mantra twenty-one times.
One becomes beloved by all people.
One should apply collyrium, tagara, kuṣṭha, vacā, lotus filaments, gorocanā, and elephant ichor, having consecrated them eight thousand times;
one will become dear to everyone.
Having fashioned an image made of salt, what do they accomplish by means of the previously mentioned rite?
Furthermore, having fashioned a jewel made of fresh butter and established it upon four leaves of the *aśvattha* tree, one should recite the mantra until it emits heat;
then, without touching it with the teeth, one should swallow it.
As soon as it is swallowed, whatever one contemplates arises.
One becomes able to assume any form at will and possesses the strength of ten men.

Having performed the preliminary practices for eighty thousand years, one should fast for three nights before a cloth painting on the full moon day. After making offerings of incense, flowers, and so forth at a shrine containing relics, one should place a sword made of *kuśa* grass upon a *raśvartha* leaf and grasp it by the hilt.
One should recite until [the deity] vibrates.
Having grasped it, one becomes a *vidyādhara*.

Before the cloth-painting (*paṭa*), during the fortnight of miracles (*prātihārakapakṣa*), bathing three times a day, changing clothes three times, and reciting eight thousand [times] at the three junctions of the day; this is the mantra recitation.

Up until the full moon day, having fasted for three nights at the end [of that period], one should prepare a *saṅghāṭī* robe, smear it with all kinds of perfumes, and light eight thousand ghee lamps. Seated in the *paryaṅka* posture, having smeared a mandala with perfumes and placed the *saṅghāṭī* upon it, one should press down on it with the left hand and recite the mantra until it flies up.
It remains suspended at a height of seven palm trees.
Having paid homage to all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas with this very mantra, it should be received.
Upon its mere reception, one becomes a Vidyādhara;
all the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, and so forth, pay him obeisance.

Having offered various oblations before the cloth painting and performed a magnificent worship, one should place *rocanā* on a lotus leaf and, seated in the *paryaṅka* posture, recite the mantra until the threefold accomplishment is attained.
When it emits heat, there is the subjugation of all sentient beings, and one lives for a thousand years.
When it emits smoke, one lives for thousands of millions of years.
He travels a thousand yojanas and returns to that very same place;
untiring, he becomes invisible to all accomplished masters (siddhas) by means of his mind.
He produces food by means of the mind.

Then he blazes with the color of the rising sun; he is sixteen years of age, his hair is curled and coiled like a topknot, he remains for an eon, and is surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of vidyādharas. He goes wherever he desires.
For one who has performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*), there is the swaying of the garland, the increasing of the lamp-flame, the emission of rays, and the trembling of the cloth-painting.
Having seen this, whatever one seeks to accomplish is accomplished,

and there is a destruction of evil. One who desires to bring under control the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas should kindle a fire with charcoal from the khadira tree before the cloth painting and offer eight thousand oblations of salt, sesame seeds, and white mustard seeds smeared with curd, honey, and ghee, three times a day for seven nights.
They become submissive.
Having consecrated water, ashes, or mustard seeds any one of these eight thousand times, one should scatter them in the four directions;
thus the binding of the mandala is accomplished.
One should offer eight thousand oblations of milk;
one will be liberated from disease.
One who desires food should offer oblations of food.
Having ascended a mountain peak and subsisting on alms-food, one should recite the mantra three hundred thousand times.

At the conclusion, having fasted for three nights and kindled a fire with wood from the *aśvattha* tree, one should offer oblations of sesame seeds smeared with curd, honey, and ghee throughout the entire night;
one will become a king.
By means of an oblation of sesame and ghee, all aims are accomplished; one should offer honey, and one will become beloved by all people;
one should offer ghee.
If one offers milk as an oblation, one becomes radiant;
if one offers curd as an oblation, peace is attained.
Nourishment is attained.
Having kindled a fire with *sinduvāra* wood, one should offer the first portion of every cooked food;
thus, the food becomes inexhaustible as prepared.
Whoever desires the binding of the turban shall obtain it.

One should offer a hundred thousand oblations of nimba flowers; one will become beloved by all people. One should offer a hundred thousand oblations of unbroken grains of śāli rice; one will obtain a village.
Having kindled a fire with *aśoka* wood, one should offer oblations a hundred thousand times;
one will obtain sovereignty over a single region.
Reciting [the mantra] one hundred thousand times while burning *agaru* incense before the cloth painting (*paṭa*), one should perform the recitation.
Then his royal palace comes under his control.
Subsisting on alms or sacrificial food (haviṣya), he should recite the mantra forty-nine hundred thousand times;
he will obtain sovereignty over the earth.
Having subsisted on a diet of milk and barley gruel, one should recite [the mantra] eight hundred thousand times;
one should offer one hundred thousand white mustard seeds,
and one will obtain the sovereignty of a neighboring kingdom.
One should offer a hundred thousand oblations of young durvā shoots;
one will attain long life.
One should offer a hundred thousand oblations of mango leaves smeared with milk.
One is liberated from all diseases.
Having gathered all kinds of grain in one place, one should offer them into the fire one hundred thousand times;
then all the grains become inexhaustible.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of *madhūka* wood; wealth will arise.

Having combined realgar, yellow orpiment, and *daṃśarocanā*, and having consecrated it eight thousand times in front of the cloth painting, one should place it upon leaves from the wood of the Bodhi tree and recite the mantra.
It becomes effective;
whichever woman or man it is given to,
that person becomes submissive.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of clarified butter;
one obtains three villages. One should recite [the mantra] ten million times.
One becomes a vidyādhara with a retinue of one hundred;
by reciting [the mantra] one hundred thousand times,
one obtains delicious food and drink without having to ask for them.
The lord of the seven islands comes under one's control;
by offering one hundred thousand oblations of *arka* wood fuel,
one receives the binding of a royal turban.
One removes eye disease by means of the *apāmārjana* rite.
For one suffering from fever, there is the *apāmārjana* with *kuśa* grass.
One should tie on a thread spun by a maiden that has been recited over one hundred times.
One becomes fortunate.

Desiring to accomplish the ointment (*añjana*), one should take a *pala* of *sauvīrāñjana*, heat it over a fire until it emits fragrance, and purify it through the preliminary rites of ointment preparation. During a lunar eclipse, one should enter the water and recite the mantra until a *kūṣmāṇḍa* appears;
at that very moment, it bursts open.
As soon as this powder is applied, one becomes radiant;
wearing earrings and a crown, invincible to all vidyādharas, with unimpeded movement, he flies up together with his retinue and lives for five thousand years.
One should offer a hundred thousand oblations of lotuses or blue lotuses;
one obtains a thousand pieces of gold.
One should offer a hundred thousand oblations of *palāśa* wood fuel.
One obtains a thousand pieces of gold.
Having fasted for three nights and subsisted on a diet of milk and barley gruel, one should prepare the rite.
Taking one *pala* of realgar (*manaḥśilā*), one should place it upon seven *aśvattha* leaves and recite the mantra until it bursts into flames.
Having torn open his body, he should cast [the substance] inside;
at that very moment, he emerges and becomes a vidyādhara.

Possessing an unimpeded divine, stainless ear and the speed of thought, with a complexion like the rising sun, highly esteemed by all the *vidyādharas*, possessing divine movement, and surrounded by a retinue of one hundred *vidyādharas*— having performed a grand worship with perfumes and flowers before the cloth painting, subsisting on milk and barley-gruel and wearing clean garments and underclothes, whatever one prays for, that one obtains. During a lunar eclipse, having performed worship beneath a Bodhi tree with perfumes, flowers, and incense, one should recite the mantra twenty-one times over realgar and yellow orpiment and smear it upon the head.
One should apply a tilaka on the forehead;
one may enter the royal court and become a favorite of the king.
One should offer eight thousand oblations of lotus seeds smeared with curd, honey, and ghee;
whoever's name is invoked therein becomes subject to one's will.
A celibate practitioner who has conquered his senses should perform a homa of agallochum and frankincense.
On the full moon day, one should bathe a king or a person of royal rank with four jars filled with water that have been consecrated eight thousand times;
he will become illustrious.
